points.en: **Hart's question (pp. 1-4):** what is the real object of the wonder in which, as Plato and Aristotle said, philosophy begins? **Thesis:** wonder is not curiosity about a missing fact but astonishment that anything exists at all; existence is an ontological, not merely aetiological, mystery that no purely physical explanation can answer (Hart pp. 1-4).
points.zh: 哈特（**Hart**）的问题（第 1–4 页）：柏拉图和亚里士多德说哲学开始于惊奇，这种惊奇真正的对象是什么？论点：惊奇（**wonder**）不是对缺少的某个事实的好奇，而是对“竟然有东西存在”的惊讶；存在是存在论的（**ontological**）之谜，不只是因果的（**aetiological**）之谜，任何单纯物理的解释都回答不了（哈特第 1–4 页）。

points.en: **Hart's main argument (pp. 2-4, 7):** P1 what a thing is (its essence) never explains that it is (its existence), and nothing can give itself existence; P2 so the world is absolutely contingent; P3 physical (aetiological) explanations only explain one contingent thing by another, even when they reach subatomic particles or the initial singularity; C so the question of how anything that lacks inherent necessity can exist at all is ontological, and no physical explanation can answer it.
points.zh: 哈特的主论证（第 2–4、7 页）：P1 一个东西“是什么”（本质）解释不了它“存在着”（存在），没有东西能让自己存在；P2 所以世界是绝对偶然的（**absolute contingency**）；P3 物理的（因果的）解释只是用一个偶然之物解释另一个，追到亚原子粒子或初始奇点也一样；C 所以“没有内在必然性的东西怎么可能存在”是存在论的问题，任何物理解释都回答不了。

points.en: **Russell's question (p. 1):** what is philosophy worth, and why study it when it gives no definite answers? **Thesis:** its value is indirect, through its effects on those who study it, and lies only among the goods of the mind; it lies largely in its uncertainty and in the greatness of the universe it contemplates, so philosophy should be studied for its questions, not for definite answers (Russell pp. 1-7).
points.zh: 罗素（**Bertrand Russell**）的问题（第 1 页）：哲学有什么价值？它给不出确定的答案，为什么还要学？论点：哲学的价值是间接的（**indirect value**），通过它对学习者的影响实现，而且只在心灵的好处（**goods of the mind**）之中；它的价值很大程度上在于它的不确定性，以及它所沉思的宇宙的伟大；所以学哲学是为了它的问题，而不是为了确定的答案（罗素第 1–7 页）。

points.en: **Russell's main argument (pp. 3-4):** P1 a person with no philosophy is imprisoned in prejudices from common sense, from his age or nation and from convictions his reason never examined, so the world seems definite, finite and obvious to him; P2 philosophy shows that even everyday things raise problems that can be answered only very incompletely; P3 it cannot tell us the true answers with certainty, but it suggests many possibilities that widen our thinking and free it from the tyranny of custom; C so it lowers our certainty about what things are, increases our knowledge of what they may be, removes arrogant dogmatism and keeps wonder alive: its value lies largely in its uncertainty.
points.zh: 罗素的主论证（第 3–4 页）：P1 没有哲学的人被关在偏见里，偏见来自常识、他的时代或国家、以及理性从没检查过的看法，世界在他眼里确定、有限、一目了然；P2 哲学表明，连最日常的东西也会引出只能很不完整地回答的问题；P3 哲学不能确定地告诉我们真正的答案，却能提出许多可能性，扩大我们的思想，把它从习俗的暴政（**tyranny of custom**）中解放出来；C 所以哲学减少我们对“事物是什么”的确定感，增加我们对“事物可能是什么”的知识，去掉傲慢的独断（**arrogant dogmatism**），让惊奇保持活力：哲学的价值在很大程度上就在它的不确定性之中。

points.en: **Wonder vs curiosity (pp. 1-2):** curiosity wants a fact we do not yet have and ends when we find it; wonder is the sudden awareness that no fact could explain the mystery that anything exists. Hart suggests that small children feel the world's givenness more openly, while adults let habit replace awe. He quotes Angelus Silesius: "The rose is without 'why'" (p. 2).
points.zh: 惊奇与好奇（第 1–2 页）：好奇想要一个还不知道的事实，找到了就结束；惊奇是突然意识到：任何事实都解释不了“竟然有东西存在”这个谜。哈特认为小孩子也许更能敞开地感受到世界的被给予性（**givenness**），大人却让习惯取代了敬畏。他引用 **Angelus Silesius** 的诗句：“玫瑰没有为什么”（第 2 页）。

points.en: **'What it is' vs 'that it is' (pp. 2-3):** in rare adult moments the familiar world suddenly seems strange, and we see that a thing's essence ('what it is') has no logical link to its existence ('that it is') (p. 2). Nothing we know is owed its existence or can bring itself into being (gratuitous existence), so the world cannot explain why it exists. Hart describes this as a strange happiness, not loss: one feels close to a great discovery.
points.zh: “是什么”与“存在着”（第 2–3 页）：在难得的瞬间，熟悉的世界忽然显得陌生，我们看到一个东西的本质（“是什么”）和它的存在（“存在着”）之间没有逻辑联系（第 2 页）。我们知道的东西没有一样是理应存在的，也没有一样能让自己存在（无端的存在，**gratuitous existence**），所以世界解释不了自己为什么存在。哈特说这种体验是一种奇特的快乐，不是失落，像站在一个大发现的边上。

points.en: **Absolute contingency; ontological vs aetiological (pp. 4, 7):** "The world need not be thus" (p. 4): it could have been different, and it could have not existed at all. Aetiological questions ask about physical origins, earlier physical states, persistence through time and the physical parts of the universe; the ontological question asks how anything that lacks inherent necessity can exist at all. Tracing causes down to the subatomic or back to the initial singularity reaches only the most basic contingent things, so that question remains.
points.zh: 绝对偶然性；存在论的与因果的（第 4、7 页）：“世界不必是这个样子”（第 4 页）：它本来可以是别的样子，也本来可以根本不存在。因果的问题问物理起源、之前的物理状态、在时间中的持续、宇宙的物理成分；存在论的问题问：没有内在必然性的东西，怎么可能存在？顺着原因往下追到亚原子、往前追到初始奇点，得到的也只是最基本的偶然之物，所以这个问题还在。“偶然”不是“随机”或“不重要”。

points.en: **Taylor's sphere (pp. 4-5):** Richard Taylor imagines a walker who finds a large translucent sphere in a forest; he would find it absurd that it is there with no cause. The same question fits a rock or a tree, and only familiarity stops us asking it; a sphere as big as the universe or as small as a grain of sand, lasting forever or only a moment, raises it just as much. So what calls for explanation is a thing's sheer 'thereness', its existence and not only its nature.
points.zh: 泰勒的圆球（第 4–5 页）：理查德·泰勒（**Richard Taylor**）设想一个人在森林里发现一个半透明的大圆球，他会觉得它没有原因就在那儿很荒唐。同样的问题也适用于一块石头、一棵树，只是熟悉让我们不问；圆球像宇宙那么大或像沙粒那么小、永远存在或只存在一瞬间，问题都一样。所以需要解释的是一个东西赤裸裸地“就在那儿”（**thereness**），即它的存在，而不只是它的本性。

points.en: **Ontological poverty (pp. 5-7):** everything we can sense or imagine is impermanent ('annicha', a Buddhist term Hart borrows), composite and so able to fall apart, and subject to time, always becoming something else. In every finite thing essence and existence are joined and neither explains the other; even what I am and that I am come from outside me. So no finite thing has the ground of its being in itself, and nature as a whole receives its being. 'Poverty' means total dependence for existence, not lack of money.
points.zh: 存在上的贫乏（**ontological poverty**，第 5–7 页）：我们能感到、能想到的一切都是无常的（**annicha**，哈特借用的佛教词）、复合的（所以会散掉）、受时间支配而总在变成别的东西。每个有限的东西都结合了本质和存在，谁也解释不了谁；连“我是什么”和“我存在”也来自我之外。所以没有任何有限的东西在自身之内拥有存在的根据，整个自然都是接受存在的。“贫乏”指存在上的彻底依赖，不是没钱。

points.en: **Explaining it away, and Hart's reply (pp. 3-4):** the moment cannot last, because its object is the existence of the world as such and it is far from practical life, so we return to habitual single-mindedness. People explain this 'ontological surprise' away as a brain glitch (like déjà vu), as a false question produced by loose grammar, or as unintelligible. Hart replies that these moves come from the need to get on with life, not from an answer: they abandon the responsibility to think (p. 4).
points.zh: 三种“打发”方式与哈特的回应（第 3–4 页）：这种瞬间留不住：它的对象是世界的存在本身，又离实际生活太远，所以我们回到习惯性的“一心只顾眼前”（**single-mindedness**）。有人把这种存在论的惊讶（**ontological surprise**）说成像似曾相识那样的大脑故障，有人说存在的问题是不严谨的语法造出来的假问题，还有人说它根本说不通。哈特回应：这些做法来自继续过日子的需要，不是回答了问题，而是放弃了思考的责任（第 4 页）。

points.en: **Three paths and the question of God (pp. 7-8):** reflection on contingency can follow the chain of causes back, look for a stable shore beyond change, or turn to the unity that holds all things together. Each path tempts us to shrink being into a simple concept, since beings are easier to think about than being as such. Reason cannot leave the question alone, so a rational life must keep asking the question of God, which differs in kind from questions about the gods within nature. Hart gives no proof that God exists, and the selection breaks off mid-sentence (p. 8).
points.zh: 三条思路与上帝的问题（第 7–8 页）：思考偶然性可以沿因果链往回追，可以去找变化之外那片“稳定的岸”，也可以转向把万物维系在一起的统一。每条路都诱使我们把存在缩成一个简单概念，因为想存在者比想存在本身容易。理性放不下这个问题，所以理性的生活必须一再追问上帝的问题（**the question of God**），它和关于自然之内诸神的问题在种类上不同。哈特没有证明上帝存在；节选在半句话处中断（第 8 页）。

points.en: **Objections to Hart (the station's assessment):** (1) his argument assumes that whatever is contingent needs an explanation, so one can grant that everything is contingent and still say the universe simply exists with no explanation; (2) Taylor's sphere may borrow our knowledge that ordinary objects have makers; (3) what holds of every part (dependence) need not hold of the whole, as every brick may be small while the wall is large. Hart's best support is the sphere: size and age make no difference. Outside the reading: the reply in (1) is often called the 'brute fact' reply.
points.zh: 对哈特的反驳（本站的理解）：①他的论证默认“偶然的东西都需要解释”，有人可以承认万物都偶然，却说宇宙就是存在着、没有解释；②泰勒的圆球也许借用了“普通物体都有制造者”的背景知识；③每一部分都依赖，推不出整体也依赖，就像每块砖都小，墙却可以很大。哈特最好的支持是圆球：大小和存在多久都不影响问题。补充（读物外）：①这种回应常叫“原始事实”（**brute fact**）回应。

points.en: **Indirect value and the 'practical' person (pp. 1-2):** physical science is useful through its inventions even to people who know nothing about it; philosophy is not, so its value for others can only be indirect, through the lives of those who study it. The 'practical' person (in Russell's scare quotes) sees only the body's needs and forgets that the mind needs food too; even a world without poverty and disease would still need the goods of the mind.
points.zh: 间接价值与所谓“务实”的人（第 1–2 页）：物理科学通过发明，对完全不懂它的人也有用；哲学没有这种效用，所以它对别人的价值只能是间接的，通过学习者的生活实现。所谓“务实”的人（**practical person**，罗素加了引号）只看到身体的需要，忘了心灵也需要食粮；就算没有贫穷和疾病，世界也还需要心灵的好处。

points.en: **The residue argument (the station's label) and insoluble questions (pp. 2-3):** philosophy aims at knowledge, but once definite knowledge of a subject becomes possible, the subject becomes a separate science, as astronomy and psychology did; what keeps the name 'philosophy' is the residue of unanswered questions, so its uncertainty is largely more apparent than real. Russell adds that this is only part of the truth: some questions (Is the universe planned or a chance collection of atoms? Is consciousness permanent? Do good and evil matter to the universe?) seem insoluble, yet philosophy must keep our speculative interest in the universe alive.
points.zh: “剩余物”论证（本站的叫法）与无解之问（第 2–3 页）：哲学追求知识，但一门学问一旦能得到确定的知识，就成为独立的科学，天文学和心理学就是这样；留下来仍叫“哲学”的，是还答不了的剩余问题（**residue**），所以哲学的不确定在很大程度上是表面的多于真实的。罗素补充：这只是一部分真相；有些问题（宇宙有计划，还是原子的偶然聚合？意识会永存吗？善恶对宇宙重要吗？）似乎无解，但哲学要让我们对宇宙的思辨兴趣保持活力。

points.en: **Contemplation: Self and not-Self (pp. 4-5):** the instinctive person's life is shut inside private interests, like a garrison in a besieged fortress that knows it must surrender. Philosophic contemplation views the universe impartially, not as friends and enemies, and so enlarges the Self, best when this is not directly sought: we start from the not-Self and adapt ourselves to what we find. Self-assertion, such as trying to prove that the world is like us, blocks this growth; Russell rejects the popular view on which humanity is the measure of all things.
points.zh: 沉思：自我与非我（第 4–5 页）：本能式的人（**instinctive person**）的生活被关在私人利益里，像被围困的要塞里知道迟早要投降的守军。哲学的沉思（**philosophic contemplation**）不偏不倚地看宇宙，不分敌我，因而扩大自我；而且最好的扩大不是刻意求来的：从非我出发，让自我去适应它发现的东西（**Self and not-Self**）。自我主张（**self-assertion**），比如想证明世界和我们相像，会阻碍这种成长；罗素反对“人是万物的尺度”这种流行观点。

points.en: **The free intellect and citizens of the universe (pp. 5-7):** the free intellect sees "as God might see" (p. 6), a metaphor for impartiality (an interpretation): free of a personal here and now, of hopes and fears, and of customary beliefs. The same impartiality is the desire for truth in contemplation, justice in action and universal love in emotion, and through it we become citizens of the universe rather than of a single walled city fighting all the others. Final summary: the questions widen our sense of what is possible and weaken dogmatic confidence; above all, the mind becomes great and capable of union with the universe, its highest good.
points.zh: 自由的理智与宇宙公民（第 5–7 页）：自由的理智（**free intellect**）“像上帝那样看”（第 6 页），按本站的理解，这是比喻不偏不倚：没有个人的此时此地，没有希望和恐惧，也没有习惯的成见。同一种不偏不倚（**impartiality**），在沉思中是求真的愿望，在行动中是正义，在情感中是普遍的爱，它让我们成为宇宙公民（**citizens of the universe**），而不只是一座与别城交战的围城里的公民。总结：哲学的问题扩大我们对“什么是可能的”的看法，削弱独断的自信；最重要的是让心灵变得伟大，能和宇宙结合，这是心灵的至善。

points.en: **Hart and Russell compared (an interpretation):** both link philosophy to wonder at familiar things, both see habit or custom as its enemy, and both value questions that may never be answered. But Hart's wonder is about existence itself and claims a glimpse of a truth (absolute contingency) that leads to the question of God, while Russell's wonder comes from new possibilities and the greatness of the universe, he holds that definite answers usually cannot be known to be true, and his God is only an image of impartiality.
points.zh: 哈特与罗素对比（本站的理解）：两人都把哲学和对熟悉事物的惊奇联系起来，都认为习惯或习俗是惊奇的敌人，也都看重也许永远没有答案的问题。不同：哈特的惊奇针对存在本身，自认瞥见了一个真理（绝对偶然性），并走向上帝的问题；罗素的惊奇来自新的可能性和宇宙的伟大，他认为确定的答案通常无法被知道为真，他说的上帝只是不偏不倚的比喻。

formulas.expr:
what it is (essence) does not explain that it is (existence)
→ absolute contingency: the world could have been otherwise, or not at all
→ the mystery of existence is ontological, not merely aetiological
formulas.en: The skeleton of Hart's argument (Hart pp. 2-4, 7). Its unstated premise, that whatever is contingent calls for an explanation, is where critics attack (an interpretation).
formulas.zh: 哈特论证的骨架（第 2–4、7 页）。它没明说的前提是“偶然的东西需要解释”，反驳者正是从这里下手（本站的理解）。

formulas.expr:
less certainty about what things are + more knowledge of what they may be
→ freedom from the tyranny of custom, no arrogant dogmatism, wonder kept alive
formulas.en: Why Russell says philosophy's value lies largely in its uncertainty (Russell pp. 3-4).
formulas.zh: 罗素：哲学的价值为什么很大程度上就在它的不确定性之中（第 3–4 页）。

formulas.expr:
impartiality: in contemplation = the desire for truth | in action = justice | in emotion = universal love
→ citizens of the universe
formulas.en: One quality of mind, three forms (Russell p. 6); on the station's reading, seeing "as God might see" is a metaphor for it.
formulas.zh: 同一种不偏不倚，在沉思、行动、情感中分别是求真、正义、普遍的爱（罗素第 6 页）；按本站的理解，“像上帝那样看”只是它的比喻。

points.en: **Apology: the speech and its thesis (pp. 1-4):** Plato's Apology (trans. Grube) is Socrates' defence speech at his trial (apologia means a defence, not saying sorry). **Thesis:** his only wisdom is human wisdom: he does not think he knows what he does not know; his questioning of people is service to the god, and he will obey the god rather than stop, even facing death.
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：辩护词与论点（第 1–4 页）：柏拉图（**Plato**）的《申辩篇》（**Apology**，Grube 译）是苏格拉底（**Socrates**）在审判中的辩护词（apologia 是“辩护”，不是“道歉”）。论点：他唯一的智慧是人的智慧（**human wisdom**）：不以为自己知道自己不知道的事；他盘问别人是在为神服务；他宁可服从神，也不停止哲学，哪怕面对死亡。

points.en: **Apology: the oracle argument (pp. 3-4, 21a-23b):** P1 the oracle at Delphi told Chairephon that no one was wiser than Socrates; P2 Socrates knew he was not wise, and the god does not lie, so the answer was a riddle; P3 he questioned politicians, poets and craftsmen, and each thought he knew important things he did not know (the craftsmen did know their crafts); P4 Socrates does not think he knows what he does not know; C so he is wiser only in this small way, and the oracle means that human wisdom is of little or no value.
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：神谕论证（第 3–4 页，21a–23b）：P1 德尔斐神谕回答凯勒丰（**Chairephon**）：没有人比苏格拉底更有智慧；P2 苏格拉底知道自己并不智慧，而神不会说谎，所以这是一个需要解读的谜；P3 他盘问政治家、诗人、工匠，发现每个人都以为自己懂重要的事，其实不懂（工匠确实懂自己的手艺）；P4 苏格拉底不以为自己知道自己不知道的事；C 所以他只在这一小点上更智慧，神谕的意思是：人的智慧价值很小甚至没有。

points.en: **Euthyphro: the question (pp. 4-5, 5c-6e):** what is piety (the pious)? Socrates asks for "that form itself" (p. 5, 6d): the one form that makes every pious action pious, to be used as a model for judging any action. **Outcome:** every definition Euthyphro offers fails, and the dialogue ends without one when he leaves in a hurry (p. 11).
points.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》：问题（第 4–5 页，5c–6e）：什么是虔敬（**piety**）？苏格拉底要的是“那个型本身”（第 5 页，6d）：让所有虔敬行为都虔敬的那一个型（形式，**form**），好拿它当范本判断任何行为。结果：游叙弗伦（**Euthyphro**）给出的定义一个个失败，他说有急事离开，对话没有得出定义（第 11 页）。

points.en: **Euthyphro: the dilemma (pp. 6-8, 9e-11b):** P1 D3: whatever all the gods love is pious (the god-loved); P2 a thing is affected because something affects it (carried, led, seen), so the god-loved is god-loved because the gods love it; P3 Euthyphro agrees that the gods love the pious because it is pious; P4 if the pious and the god-loved were the same, swapping one for the other would contradict P2 or P3; C so they are not the same: being loved by all the gods is only "an affect or a quality" of the pious (p. 8, 11a), not what it is. Outside the reading: this question is now called the Euthyphro dilemma.
points.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》：两难论证（第 6–8 页，9e–11b）：P1 D3：虔敬就是所有神都爱的东西（为神所爱的，**god-loved**）；P2 被作用的东西是因为有东西作用它才被作用（被搬、被领、被看），所以为神所爱的之所以为神所爱，是因为神爱它；P3 游叙弗伦同意：神爱虔敬的东西，是因为它虔敬；P4 如果虔敬和为神所爱的是同一个东西，互换之后就会和 P2 或 P3 矛盾；C 所以二者不同：被所有神爱只是虔敬的“一种遭受或性质”（第 8 页，11a），不是它的本质。补充（读物外）：这个问题后人叫“游叙弗伦困境”（**Euthyphro dilemma**）。

points.en: **Apology: two sets of accusers (pp. 1-4):** the old accusers' rumours (studying the heavens and what lies under the earth, making the worse argument the stronger, teaching for fees) are more dangerous than the formal charge, because jurors heard them as children and no one ever answered them. The formal charge of Meletus, Anytus and Lycon: corrupting the young and not believing in the city's gods but in new spiritual things (p. 4, 24b-c). Socrates says the slander and envy of many people, not Meletus, will convict him (28a).
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：两批控告者（第 1–4 页）：早先控告者的流言（研究天上地下、把较弱的论证说成较强的、收费教人）比正式指控更危险，因为陪审员小时候就听过，又一直没人反驳。美勒托（**Meletus**）、安尼图斯（**Anytus**）、吕孔（**Lycon**）的正式指控：败坏青年；不信城邦的神，而信新的精灵之事（第 4 页，24b–c）。苏格拉底说，真正会让他被定罪的是很多人的诽谤和嫉妒，而不是美勒托（28a）。

points.en: **Apology: cross-examining Meletus (pp. 5-7, 24c-28a):** (1) Meletus says all Athenians improve the young and only Socrates corrupts them, but horses are improved by one or a few experts (horse breeders) and made worse by most users, so Meletus has never cared about the young; (2) bad people harm those close to them, so no one corrupts his companions deliberately, and an unwilling wrongdoer should be instructed, not prosecuted; (3) believing in spiritual things means believing in spirits, who are gods or children of gods, as no one believes in mules without horses and asses, so Meletus contradicts himself. They expose Meletus' carelessness but do not answer the charge about the city's gods.
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：盘问美勒托（第 5–7 页，24c–28a）：①美勒托说所有雅典人都让青年变好，只有苏格拉底败坏他们；可马只有一个或极少数专家（养马人）能养好，大多数使用者反而养坏，所以美勒托从没关心过青年；②坏人会伤害身边的人，所以没人会故意败坏同伴；无意犯错的人应该私下教导，不该起诉；③信精灵之事就得信有精灵，精灵是神或神的孩子，就像没人信有骡子却不信有马和驴，所以美勒托自相矛盾。这些论证揭露了美勒托的马虎，却没回应“不信城邦的神”这一条。

points.en: **Apology: the post and the fear of death (p. 7, 28b-29b):** like Achilles, and like Socrates himself at Potidaea, Amphipolis and Delium, a man must stay at his post, and Socrates believes the god stationed him in philosophy. No one knows whether death is a great good or a great evil, so fearing death is thinking one knows what one does not know, the most blameworthy ignorance. Yet Socrates does claim to know that doing wrong and disobeying a superior, god or man, is shameful (29b), so human wisdom is not 'I know nothing'.
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：坚守岗位与怕死（第 7 页，28b–29b）：像阿喀琉斯（**Achilles**）一样，也像苏格拉底自己在波提狄亚、安菲波利斯、德利乌姆那样，人必须守住岗位；苏格拉底相信神把他安排在哲学这个岗位上。没人知道死是最大的好事还是最大的坏事，所以怕死就是以为自己知道自己不知道的事，这是最该受责备的无知，也就是假智慧（**false wisdom**）。可苏格拉底确实说自己知道：做错事、不服从上级（神或人）是可耻的（29b），所以人的智慧不等于“我什么都不知道”。

points.en: **Apology: obeying the god; the gadfly (pp. 7-9, 29c-31c):** if acquitted on condition that he stop philosophizing, he would refuse: "I will obey the god rather than you" (p. 8, 29d), and he would keep urging everyone to care for wisdom, truth and the soul more than for wealth or reputation. A worse man cannot harm a better one, so killing him would harm the jurors more. He is a gadfly that the god attached to the city, a large but sluggish horse; his poverty shows that he never took fees.
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：服从神与牛虻（第 7–9 页，29c–31c）：如果以“不再搞哲学”为条件释放他，他会拒绝：“我要服从神，而不是服从你们”（第 8 页，29d），并继续劝每个人关心智慧、真理和灵魂，胜过钱财和名声。坏人不能伤害比他好的人，所以杀他伤害陪审员自己更多。他是神安在城邦这匹又大又懒的马身上的牛虻（**gadfly**）；他的贫穷证明他从不收费。

points.en: **Apology: the divine sign and the private life (pp. 9-10, 31c-33a):** since childhood Socrates has had a divine sign, a voice that only turns him away from what he is about to do; it kept him out of politics, because a man who really fights injustice in public life will not survive. Evidence in deeds: he opposed the illegal trial of the generals under the democracy and refused the Thirty's order to arrest Leon of Salamis under the oligarchy. The sign is not the oracle.
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：神圣征兆与私人生活（第 9–10 页，31c–33a）：苏格拉底从小就有神圣征兆（**divine sign**），一个只会阻止他、从不鼓励他的声音；它让他远离政治，因为在公共生活中真正反对不义的人活不下去。行动证据：民主制下他反对非法审判将军们，寡头制下他拒绝三十人（**the Thirty**）逮捕萨拉米斯的勒翁（**Leon**）的命令。征兆不是神谕。

points.en: **Apology: no pity, the counter-penalty, the unexamined life (pp. 10-12, 34b-38b):** he will not beg or parade his children, since that shames the city and asks jurors to break their oath. Convicted by a margin of only thirty votes, he proposes free meals in the Prytaneum (more fitting for him than for an Olympic victor), rejects prison, exile and keeping quiet because "the unexamined life is not worth living" (p. 12, 38a), and finally offers a fine of thirty minae guaranteed by Plato and others; the jury sentences him to death.
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：不求情、反提刑罚与未经审视的人生（第 10–12 页，34b–38b）：他不哭求、不带孩子上庭，因为那会让城邦蒙羞，也等于要陪审员违背誓言。他以仅仅三十票之差被定罪后，提出在市政厅（**Prytaneum**）免费用餐（比给奥运冠军更合适），拒绝坐牢、流放和闭嘴，因为“未经审视的人生不值得过”（第 12 页，38a）；最后他提出三十明那的罚款，由柏拉图等人担保，陪审团判他死刑。

points.en: **Apology: after the sentence (pp. 12-14, 39a-42a):** his divine sign never opposed him that day, so what has happened is probably good. Death is either like a dreamless sleep, which would be a gain, or a move of the soul to another place, where he could meet true judges and the great poets and go on examining people; so one may hope, with good reason, that death is a blessing. He claims hope, not knowledge, which fits his earlier point that no one knows what death is (29a).
points.zh: 《申辩篇》：判决之后（第 12–14 页，39a–42a）：受审这天他的神圣征兆一次也没阻止他，所以发生的事很可能是好事。死要么像无梦的睡眠，那是收获；要么是灵魂迁居到另一个地方，在那里能见到真正的法官和伟大的诗人，还能继续审视别人；所以有理由怀着美好的希望：死是一件好事。他主张的是希望，不是知识，这和他前面说的“没人知道死是什么”一致（29a）。

points.en: **Euthyphro: the case and D1 (pp. 2-5):** Euthyphro is prosecuting his own father for the death of a laborer who had himself killed a household slave, and he claims exact knowledge of piety. D1, that the pious is doing what Euthyphro is doing now, prosecuting wrongdoers whoever they are, fails because it gives one example, not the form: a list of examples is not a definition.
points.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》：案子与 D1（第 2–5 页）：游叙弗伦为一个雇工的死告自己的父亲，而这个雇工自己先杀了家里的一个奴隶；游叙弗伦自称准确知道什么是虔敬。D1：虔敬就是做他现在做的事，起诉做错事的人，不管是谁。它失败，因为只举了一个例子，没说出型（形式）：列例子不等于下定义。

points.en: **Euthyphro: D2 and the quarrelling gods (pp. 5-6, 6e-9e):** D2: the pious is whatever is dear to the gods. Disputes about number, size and weight are settled by counting, measuring and weighing; only disputes about the just, the beautiful and the good lead to hatred, so these are what the quarrelling gods disagree about. Then the same act (Euthyphro punishing his father) may please Zeus but displease Cronus, and would be both pious and impious; D2 fails. Socrates' amendment D3: whatever all the gods love is pious.
points.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》：D2 与诸神之争（第 5–6 页，6e–9e）：D2：神所喜爱的就是虔敬的。关于数目、大小、轻重的分歧，数一数、量一量、称一称就解决了；只有关于正义、美、好的分歧才引起仇恨，所以诸神争吵的正是这些。那么同一个行为（游叙弗伦惩罚父亲）可能让宙斯高兴、让克洛诺斯不高兴，于是既虔敬又不虔敬；D2 失败。苏格拉底提出修正 D3：虔敬就是所有神都爱的。

points.en: **Euthyphro: care and service (pp. 8-10, 11e-14c):** piety is a part of justice (everything pious is just, but not everything just is pious, as shame is a part of fear and odd a part of number). D4, care of the gods, fails because care improves its object (horses, dogs, cattle) and nothing we do makes a god better; as service to the gods it fails because Euthyphro cannot name the main product the gods achieve through our service, as doctors achieve health and shipbuilders ships.
points.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》：照料与服侍（第 8–10 页，11e–14c）：虔敬是正义的一部分（虔敬的都是正义的，正义的不都是虔敬的，就像羞耻是恐惧的一部分、奇数是数的一部分）。D4“照料神”（**care of the gods**）失败，因为照料会让对象变好（马、狗、牛），而我们做的事不能让神变好；改成“服侍神”（**service to the gods**）后，游叙弗伦说不出神靠我们的服侍完成的主要产物，而医生完成的是健康，造船匠完成的是船。

points.en: **Euthyphro: trade and the circle (pp. 10-11, 14c-16a):** D5: piety is knowing how to sacrifice (giving to the gods) and pray (asking from them). Then piety would be "a sort of trading skill" (p. 10, 14e); but the gods gain nothing from our gifts, which are only honour, reverence and what pleases them, so the pious turns out to be what is dearest to the gods, the definition already refuted. The argument has gone in a circle; Socrates wants to start again from the beginning, but Euthyphro leaves.
points.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》：交易与绕回原点（第 10–11 页，14c–16a）：D5：虔敬就是懂得献祭（给神东西）和祈祷（向神要东西）。这样虔敬就成了“一种交易技艺”（**trading skill**，第 10 页，14e）；可神从我们的礼物里得不到好处，得到的只是尊敬、敬畏和让神高兴的东西，于是虔敬又成了“对神最可爱的”，也就是已经被驳倒的定义：论证绕了一圈回到原点。苏格拉底想从头再来，游叙弗伦却走了。

points.en: **The two dialogues compared (an interpretation):** Euthyphro, who claims exact knowledge of piety and acts on it against his own father but cannot define it, illustrates the Apology's most blameworthy ignorance: thinking one knows what one does not know. Socrates calls his questioning service to the god; in the Euthyphro, piety as service fails only because Euthyphro cannot name its product. Both dialogues compare moral questions with crafts (horse breeders; caring for horses and dogs), which the station calls craft analogies, and neither reaches a final definition. In story order the Euthyphro comes before the trial.
points.zh: 两篇对比（本站的理解）：游叙弗伦自称准确知道虔敬、并据此告自己的父亲，却说不出定义，正好印证《申辩篇》说的最该受责备的无知：以为自己知道自己不知道的事。苏格拉底把盘问叫作为神服务；《游叙弗伦篇》里“服侍神”失败，只是因为说不出它的产物。两篇都拿技艺来比道德问题（养马人；照料马和狗），即技艺类比（**craft analogy**，本站的叫法），两篇也都没有得出最终定义。按故事时间，《游叙弗伦篇》发生在审判之前。

points.en: **Labels from outside the readings:** outside the reading, Socrates' question-and-answer testing is often called the elenchus, his divine sign the daimonion, the 10a question the Euthyphro dilemma (later generalized as: is an act right because God commands it, or commanded because it is right? divine command theory takes the first horn), and an ending without an answer aporia. Grube's translation uses none of these, so give the reading's wording too. Socrates never says 'I know that I know nothing' in this reading.
points.zh: 补充（读物外）：苏格拉底一问一答的检验后人常叫 **elenchus**（诘问法），神圣征兆常叫 **daimonion**，10a 的问题叫“游叙弗伦困境”（**Euthyphro dilemma**；后人推广成“对的事是因为神命令才对，还是本来就对、神才命令”，选前一支的叫神命论 **divine command theory**），无解的结尾叫 **aporia**（困惑）。Grube 的译文一个都没用，答题时要同时写出读物的说法。苏格拉底在这篇里也从没说过“我知道我一无所知”。

formulas.expr:
Meletus: all Athenians improve the young, only Socrates corrupts them
horses: one or a few experts improve them, most users make them worse
→ Meletus has never thought about the young (25a-c)
formulas.en: The first argument against Meletus attacks his credibility, not the charge itself (Apology p. 5).
formulas.zh: 驳美勒托的第一个论证（第 5 页）：打击的是美勒托的可信度，不是指控本身。

formulas.expr:
no one knows whether death is good or bad (29a)
fearing death = acting as if one knew it is the worst evil = false wisdom
but Socrates knows that doing wrong and disobeying a superior is shameful (29b)
formulas.en: Human wisdom applied to death (Apology p. 7): not pretending to know is different from knowing nothing.
formulas.zh: 把人的智慧用在死亡上（第 7 页）：不装作知道，不等于什么都不知道。

formulas.expr:
D1 an example: prosecuting wrongdoers → D2 dear to the gods → D3 loved by all the gods
→ D4 care of the gods, then service to the gods → D5 knowing how to sacrifice and pray (a trading skill)
→ back to 'dearest to the gods'
formulas.en: Euthyphro's definitions in order (Euthyphro pp. 4-11): D2 falls to the quarrelling gods, D3 to the dilemma, D4 to care and the missing product, D5 to the circle.
formulas.zh: 游叙弗伦的定义顺序（第 4–11 页）：D2 被诸神之争驳倒，D3 被两难驳倒，D4 败在照料和说不出产物，D5 绕回原点。

points.en: **Meno's question (pp. 2-3, 70a-71b):** Meno asks whether virtue can be taught, or is gained by practice, or is present by nature, or comes some other way. Socrates says he cannot tell, because he does not know what virtue is, and one cannot know what qualities a thing has without knowing what it is (71b): someone who has no idea who Meno is cannot know whether Meno is handsome, rich or well-born. Outside the reading: this principle is often called the priority of definition.
points.zh: 美诺的问题（第 2–3 页，70a–71b）：美诺（**Meno**）问美德（**virtue**）能不能教，还是靠练习、天生或别的方式得来。苏格拉底说他答不了，因为他不知道美德是什么，而不知道一个东西是什么，就不可能知道它有什么性质（71b）：完全不知道美诺是谁的人，没法知道他好不好看、有没有钱、出身好不好。补充（读物外）：这个原则后人常叫“定义优先”（**priority of definition**）。

points.en: **Where the dialogue ends (pp. 26-28, 97a-100b):** virtue is never defined. On the way the dialogue draws a key distinction: knowledge is true opinion tied down by an account of the reason why (98a), while true opinion guides as well as knowledge for as long as it stays. Socrates concludes, only if their inquiry was right, that good statesmen guide by right opinion, so virtue comes as a gift from the gods without understanding, and that they will know this clearly only after finding what virtue itself is (100b).
points.zh: 全篇的结局（第 26–28 页，97a–100b）：美德始终没有被定义。途中得出一个关键区分：知识（**knowledge**）是被对原因的说明拴住的真意见（98a），而真意见只要留得住，引导行动就不比知识差。苏格拉底只是有条件地（如果这场探究没错）得出：好政治家靠正确意见领导，所以美德是神的恩赐（**divine gift**），不伴随理解地到来；要清楚地知道这一点，得先弄清美德本身是什么（100b）。

points.en: **The debater's argument and recollection (pp. 10-12, 80a-81e):** after his definitions fail, Meno says Socrates numbs people like a torpedo fish. The debater's argument: one cannot search for what one knows (there is no need) or for what one does not know (one would not know what to look for), so inquiry is impossible. Socrates replies, citing priests, priestesses and poets such as Pindar, that the soul is immortal and has learned everything, so "searching and learning are, as a whole, recollection" (p. 11, 81d); believing this makes us energetic, while the debater's argument would make us idle. Outside the reading: this puzzle is usually called Meno's paradox.
points.zh: 辩论家的论证与回忆说（第 10–12 页，80a–81e）：定义都失败后，美诺说苏格拉底像电鳐（**torpedo fish**）一样把人弄麻。辩论家的论证（**debater's argument**）：已经知道的不必找，不知道的不知道要找什么，所以探究不可能。苏格拉底借祭司、女祭司和品达（**Pindar**）等诗人的说法回答：灵魂不朽，已经学过一切，所以“寻找和学习整个说来就是回忆”（第 11 页，81d）；相信这一点让人勤奋，那个论证却会让人懒惰。补充（读物外）：这个难题后人通常叫“美诺悖论”（**Meno's paradox**）。

points.en: **The slave-boy demonstration (pp. 12-16, 82b-85b):** a slave boy from Meno's household, never taught geometry, is asked for the side of a square of 8 square feet, double a 2-foot square of 4. He first doubles the side (4 feet gives 16), then tries 3 feet (9), admits he does not know, and finally sees that the square on the diagonal is the answer. Perplexity helped him: once he no longer thinks he knows, he wants to find out (84a-c). The answer is a line, not a number.
points.zh: 奴隶男孩的演示（第 12–16 页，82b–85b）：美诺家里的一个奴隶男孩，从没学过几何。问题：边长 2 英尺的正方形面积是 4 平方英尺，面积加倍（8 平方英尺）的正方形边长多少？他先把边加倍（4 英尺，得 16），再试 3 英尺（得 9），承认自己不知道，最后看出以原正方形对角线（**diagonal**）为边的正方形就是答案。困惑（**perplexity**）帮了他：不再以为自己知道，他才想弄明白（84a–c）。答案是一条线，不是一个数。

points.en: **From the demonstration to recollection and immortality (pp. 16-17, 85b-86c):** P1 the boy's answers were his own opinions, though he did not know the answer before; P2 so someone who does not know can have true opinions within him, stirred up as in a dream; P3 repeated questioning would turn them into knowledge without any teaching; P4 finding knowledge within oneself is recollection; P5 no one taught him in this life, so he learned when he was not a human being; C if the truth is always in the soul, the soul is immortal. Socrates firmly defends only the practical claim that believing in inquiry makes us better, braver and less idle (86b-c).
points.zh: 从演示到回忆和灵魂不朽（第 16–17 页，85b–86c）：P1 男孩的回答都是他自己的意见，可他原本不知道答案；P2 所以不知道的人心里也可以有真意见（**true opinion**），像梦一样刚被唤起；P3 反复提问会把它们变成知识，不需要教；P4 在自己心里找到知识就是回忆（**recollection**）；P5 这辈子没人教过他，所以是他还不是人的时候学的；C 如果真理一直在灵魂里，灵魂就不朽。苏格拉底坚决捍卫的只是实践上的结论：相信探究会让我们更好、更勇敢、不那么懒惰（86b–c）。

points.en: **Weaknesses of the demonstration (an interpretation):** many of Socrates' questions are leading yes-or-no questions, and he himself draws the diagonals; the boy may be reasoning now rather than recalling; success in geometry may not carry over to virtue; and the boy ends with true opinion, not knowledge (85c).
points.zh: 演示的弱点（本站的理解）：苏格拉底的很多问题是诱导性提问（**leading question**），对角线也是他画的；男孩也许是在现场推理，而不是回忆；几何上的成功不一定能推到美德上；而且男孩最后只有真意见，还不是知识（85c）。

points.en: **One form of virtue (pp. 3-5, 71e-74b):** Meno lists virtues by role (managing the city for a man, the household for a woman, and so on), but a list is not a definition: all bees are alike in being bees, and health is the same in a man and a woman, so all virtues share one form. Everyone is good through the same qualities, justice and moderation. 'Justice is a virtue' does not say what virtue is, just as roundness is a shape but not shape itself.
points.zh: 美德的一个型（第 3–5 页，71e–74b）：美诺按身份列美德（男人管好城邦、女人管好家务等），可清单不是定义：所有蜜蜂在“是蜜蜂”这一点上都一样，健康在男人女人身上也一样，所以所有美德共有一个型（形式，**form**）。人人都是靠同样的品质（正义和节制）变好的。“正义是一种美德”没说出美德是什么，就像圆是一种形状，却不是形状本身。

points.en: **What makes a good definition (pp. 5-7, 74b-77a):** a definition must state what is common to every case (round and straight are equally shapes), be true, and use terms the questioner already accepts. The first definition of shape (what always accompanies color) is true but fails if color is not understood; the second, that shape is the limit of a solid (p. 6), passes. A Gorgias-style definition of color, borrowing Empedocles' effluvia, only sounds impressive; Socrates calls it theatrical. Later he adds: no terms still under inquiry (79d).
points.zh: 好定义的条件（第 5–7 页，74b–77a）：定义要说出所有实例共有的东西（圆和直同样都是形状），要真，还要用提问者已经接受的词（**agreed terms**）。第一个形状定义（形状是总伴随颜色的东西）是真的，但对方不懂“颜色”就不合格；第二个定义“形状是立体的界限”（第 6 页）合格。仿高尔吉亚（**Gorgias**）的颜色定义借用恩培多克勒的流射物（**effluvia**），只是听起来厉害，苏格拉底说它像演戏。后来他又补充：不能用还在探究中的词（79d）。

points.en: **The third definition and circularity (pp. 8-10, 77b-79e):** Meno: virtue is desiring fine things and being able to get them. Since no one wants what he knows to be bad (it would make him miserable), everyone desires good things, and the definition reduces to the power to secure goods. But getting goods unjustly is not virtue, so Meno must add 'justly', which defines virtue by a part of virtue: a circular definition.
points.zh: 第三个定义与循环（第 8–10 页，77b–79e）：美诺：美德就是想要美的东西并有能力得到它们。既然没人会想要自己明知是坏的东西（那会让自己悲惨），人人都欲求好东西，定义就缩成“获得好东西的能力”。可是不公正地获取不算美德，美诺只好加上“公正地”，这就是用美德的一部分来定义美德：循环定义（**circular definition**）。

points.en: **The method of hypothesis and 'virtue is knowledge' (pp. 17-20, 86d-89c):** Socrates agrees to ask whether virtue is teachable before saying what it is, by reasoning from a hypothesis as geometers do: virtue is teachable if and only if it is knowledge. Then he argues that virtue is good and so beneficial; that health, wealth and qualities of soul such as courage benefit only when wisdom directs them (courage without understanding is mere recklessness); so virtue is wisdom, in whole or in part.
points.zh: 假设法与“美德是知识”（第 17–20 页，86d–89c）：苏格拉底同意先问美德能不能教、再问它是什么，办法是像几何学家那样从假设出发（**method of hypothesis**）：美德可教，当且仅当它是知识。接着他论证：美德是好的，所以有益（**beneficial**）；健康、财富以及勇敢这类灵魂品质，只有在智慧指导下才有益（没有理解的勇敢只是鲁莽）；所以美德是智慧，或者是智慧的全部，或者是它的一部分。

points.en: **No teachers of virtue (pp. 20-25, 89d-96d):** whatever can be taught has teachers and learners. The sophists are disputed: Anytus, later one of Socrates' accusers, condemns them without having met one, and Gorgias only promises to make people clever speakers. Good men such as Themistocles, Aristides, Pericles and Thucydides (not the historian) could not make their sons good, though they had them taught skills like horsemanship and wrestling. So virtue has no teachers, is not teachable and, on the hypothesis, is not knowledge. Weakness: it generalizes from a few cases.
points.zh: 找不到美德的老师（第 20–25 页，89d–96d）：能教的东西就有老师和学生。智者（**sophists**）有争议：安尼图斯（**Anytus**，后来控告苏格拉底的人之一）一个智者都没见过就骂他们，高尔吉亚只答应让人能说会道。地米斯托克利（**Themistocles**）、阿里斯提德、伯里克利、修昔底德（不是那位历史学家）这些好人都没能把儿子教成好人，尽管让儿子学了骑马、摔跤这类技能。所以美德没有老师、不可教，照假设也就不是知识。弱点：只从少数几个例子归纳。

points.en: **The road to Larissa (pp. 25-26, 96d-97c):** they were wrong to agree that only knowledge guides correctly. A man who knows the road to Larissa guides others there correctly, but so does a man with a correct opinion about the road who has never been there; while his opinion is correct, he is no worse a guide. Meno objects that knowledge always succeeds and opinion only sometimes; Socrates replies that a true opinion always succeeds as long as it is true.
points.zh: 去拉里萨的路（第 25–26 页，96d–97c）：他们之前同意“只有知识能正确引导”，这是错的。知道去拉里萨（**Larissa**）的路的人能把别人正确带到那里，对这条路有正确看法却从没去过的人也能；只要他的看法是对的，带路就不比有知识的人差。美诺反驳：知识总能成功，意见只是有时成功；苏格拉底回答：真意见只要还是真的，就总能成功。

points.en: **The statues of Daedalus (pp. 26-27, 97d-98b):** true opinions are fine while they stay, but like Daedalus' statues or a runaway slave they run off unless tied down; they are tied down by an account of the reason why, which Socrates says is recollection, and then they become knowledge and stay. So knowledge is worth more because it is stable, not because it gives better results. Socrates says he is only guessing about much of this, but claims to know that knowledge and right opinion differ (98b).
points.zh: 代达罗斯的雕像（第 26–27 页，97d–98b）：真意见留着时是好东西，但像代达罗斯（**Daedalus**）的雕像、逃跑的奴隶一样，不拴住就会溜走；拴住它们的是对原因的说明（**account of the reason why**），苏格拉底说这就是回忆；拴住后它们就变成知识，留在原处。所以知识更值钱是因为稳定，不是因为结果更好。苏格拉底说这里很多话只是猜测，但声称知道知识和正确意见不同（98b）。

points.en: **Virtue as a gift from the gods (pp. 27-28, 98c-100b):** only knowledge and true opinion guide correctly (what goes right by chance is not human guidance), and neither comes by nature, so the good are not good by nature; virtue is not taught, so it is not knowledge; so statesmen such as Themistocles guide by right opinion and cannot make others like themselves, just as soothsayers and prophets say many true things without knowing what they say. A statesman who could make another statesman would be like Tiresias among the dead.
points.zh: 美德是神的恩赐（第 27–28 页，98c–100b）：只有知识和真意见能正确引导（碰巧做对不算人的引导），二者都不是天生的，所以好人不是天生的；美德不可教，所以不是知识；所以地米斯托克利这样的政治家靠正确意见领导，没法让别人像自己一样，就像占卜者和先知说出许多真话，却不知道自己在说什么。能把别人也培养成政治家的政治家，就像冥界里的忒瑞西阿斯（**Tiresias**）。

points.en: **The two halves compared (an interpretation):** the first half tests definitions against the demand for one common form; the second reasons from a hypothesis. Recollection links them: the slave boy's true opinions could become knowledge through repeated questioning (85c-d), and tying down a true opinion by an account of the reason why is recollection (98a). The argument that virtue is knowledge relied on 'only wisdom guides correctly', which the road to Larissa overturns. Outside the reading: the later definition of knowledge as justified true belief is often compared with 98a.
points.zh: 前后两半对比（本站的理解）：前半篇用“要说出一个共同的型（形式）”检验定义；后半篇从假设出发推理。回忆把两半连起来：男孩的真意见可以靠反复提问变成知识（85c–d），用对原因的说明拴住真意见就是回忆（98a）。“美德是知识”的论证靠的是“只有智慧能正确引导”，而去拉里萨的路推翻了这一点。补充（读物外）：后来的认识论（**epistemology**）常把知识说成“有理由的真信念”（**justified true belief**），常拿来和 98a 比较。

formulas.expr: a good definition of X: one form common to every X + true + uses agreed terms + no terms still under inquiry
formulas.en: Socrates' tests for a definition, built up from the bees, shape and color (Meno 72a-79e).
formulas.zh: 从蜜蜂、形状、颜色得出的定义标准（72a–79e）。

formulas.expr:
2-foot square = 4 square feet; target = 8 square feet
side 4 feet → 16 (too big) | side 3 feet → 9 (too big) | side = the diagonal of the 2-foot square → 8
formulas.en: The slave boy's steps (82b-85b); in the translation an area in 'feet' means square feet.
formulas.zh: 奴隶男孩的步骤（82b–85b）；译文里说面积的“英尺”指平方英尺。

formulas.expr:
hypothesis: virtue is teachable ⇔ virtue is knowledge (87b-c)
virtue is beneficial + only wisdom makes things beneficial → virtue is wisdom (87d-89a)
no teachers → not teachable → not knowledge (89d-96c, 98e-99b)
the premise given up: only knowledge guides correctly (97b-c)
formulas.en: Why the second half seems to contradict itself, and which premise Socrates gives up (Meno pp. 17-27).
formulas.zh: 后半篇看似自相矛盾，苏格拉底放弃的前提是“只有知识能正确引导”（第 17–27 页）。

title.zh: 笛卡尔论怀疑与确定性

points.en: **Descartes' question (pp. 1, 4):** having accepted many falsehoods since childhood, can he find anything completely certain on which to build stable, lasting knowledge in the sciences? **Thesis:** even if all his former beliefs can be doubted, 'I am, I exist' must be true each time he asserts or conceives it; he is a thinking thing; and his mind is known more easily and more evidently than any body (Descartes pp. 1-9).
points.zh: 笛卡尔（**René Descartes**）的问题（第 1、4 页）：从小接受了很多错误的东西，他能不能找到一样完全确定的东西，在上面建立稳定、长久的知识？论点：即使旧信念全都可以怀疑，每当他说出或想到“我在，我存在”，它就必然为真；他是一个思维之物（**thinking thing**）；他的心灵比任何物体都更容易、更明显地被认识（笛卡尔第 1–9 页）。

points.en: **The main line (pp. 1-9):** the First Meditation raises stronger and stronger reasons for doubt (the senses, dreaming, a deceiving God or a weaker origin) and then supposes a malicious demon to resist habit; the Second finds that being deceived requires that he exists, so 'I am, I exist' survives every doubt; subtracting everything doubtful leaves only thinking; and the wax shows that even bodies are grasped by the mind alone.
points.zh: 主线（第 1–9 页）：第一沉思提出一层比一层强的怀疑理由（感官、做梦、骗人的上帝或更弱的来源），再假设一个恶魔来对抗习惯；第二沉思发现被骗也需要他存在，所以“我在，我存在”经得住一切怀疑；把一切可疑的都减掉，只剩下思维；蜡块说明连物体也只由心灵把握。

points.en: **The method (p. 1):** treat any belief that is not completely certain and indubitable like one that is plainly false: withhold assent. One reason for doubt is enough, and he need not prove the belief false, so doubting is not denying. Since checking beliefs one by one would never end, he attacks their foundations, as undermining a building's foundations brings down everything resting on them. Outside the reading: 'method of doubt' and 'foundationalism' are later labels.
points.zh: 方法（第 1 页）：对不是完全确定、无可怀疑（**certain and indubitable**）的信念，要像对明显错误的信念一样，不予同意（**withholding assent**）。一个怀疑的理由就够，不必证明它是假的，所以怀疑不等于否定。一条条检查永远做不完，所以他攻击地基：房子的地基被挖空，上面的一切就会倒下。补充（读物外）：“怀疑的方法”（**method of doubt**）和“基础主义”（**foundationalism**）都是后人的叫法。

points.en: **The senses and the madmen (pp. 1-2):** P1 what he took as most true came from or through the senses; P2 the senses sometimes deceive; P3 it is wise not to trust fully anything that has fooled us even once; C so beliefs from the senses cannot be fully trusted. But this reaches only very small or distant things, not 'I am sitting by the fire in my dressing-gown'; and Descartes refuses to compare himself with madmen who think they are kings or made of glass.
points.zh: 感官与疯子（第 1–2 页）：P1 他认为最真的东西都来自感官或经由感官；P2 感官有时会骗人；P3 明智的做法是：一个来源哪怕骗过我们一次，也不再完全相信它；C 所以来自感官的信念不能完全相信。但这只够得着很小或很远的东西，够不着“我穿着睡袍坐在火炉边”；笛卡尔也拒绝拿以为自己是国王、身体是玻璃做的疯子来比。

points.en: **The dreaming argument (p. 2):** he has often dreamt that he was sitting by the fire when he was lying undressed in bed, and even the feeling of being awake has been matched in dreams. He concludes that "there are never any sure signs" (p. 2) by which being awake can be told from being asleep. So he cannot be certain of particular sensory beliefs, even that he has hands or a body. It does not claim that he is dreaming now.
points.zh: 梦境论证（第 2 页）：他常梦见自己坐在火炉边，其实却脱了衣服躺在床上；连“我醒着”的感觉在梦里也出现过。他的结论是：“永远没有可靠的标志”能把醒和睡区分开（第 2 页）。所以他不能确定具体的感觉信念，连自己有手、有身体都不能确定。它没有说他现在就在做梦。

points.en: **The painter analogy (p. 2):** dream images are like paintings: painters build sirens and satyrs from the parts of real animals, and even a wholly new picture uses real colours. So even if eyes, heads and hands were imaginary, simpler and more universal things must be real: corporeal nature and its extension, shape, quantity (size and number), place and time. Physics, astronomy and medicine, which study composite things, are doubtful; arithmetic and geometry seem certain: awake or asleep, 2 + 3 = 5, and a square cannot have more than four sides.
points.zh: 画家类比（第 2 页）：梦里的图像像图画：画家画塞壬、萨堤尔，只是把真实动物的肢体拼在一起；就算画出全新的东西，颜色也是真的。所以即使眼睛、头、手是想象出来的，更简单、更普遍的东西（**simple and universal things**）一定是真的：物体性及其广延（**extension**）、形状、量（大小和数目）、位置和时间。研究复合事物（**composite things**）的物理学、天文学、医学是可疑的；算术和几何看起来仍然确定：不管醒着还是睡着，2 + 3 = 5，正方形的边不超过四条。

points.en: **The deceiving God (pp. 2-3):** an omnipotent God could have made it so that there is no earth, sky or extended thing while everything looks just as it does now, and could make him go wrong every time he adds two and three or counts a square's sides. If instead he came about by fate, chance or an unbroken chain of events, a weaker cause makes constant error even more likely. Either way, every former belief can properly be doubted, and this is settled before the demon appears.
points.zh: 骗人的上帝（**deceiving God**，第 2–3 页）：全能的上帝可以让大地、天空、有广延的东西统统不存在，而一切看起来仍和现在一样；也可以让他每次算 2 加 3、数正方形的边都出错。如果他不是上帝造的，而是由命运、偶然或一连串事件产生的，原因越弱，越可能一直出错。不管哪种情况，所有旧信念都可以被正当地怀疑；这在恶魔出场之前就已经确定了。

points.en: **The malicious demon (pp. 3-4):** his old, highly probable opinions keep returning through habit, so he decides to pretend for a while that they are false: he supposes a malicious demon of the greatest power and cunning, which makes all external things and his own body mere illusions. The pretense is safe because his task is knowledge, not action. The demon is a method against habit, not something he believes in; on the station's reading it adds no new reason for doubt. Outside the reading: other translations call it the 'evil demon' or 'evil genius'.
points.zh: 恶意的恶魔（**malicious demon**，第 3–4 页）：高度可能的旧意见总是靠习惯回来，所以他决定暂时假装它们都是假的：假设一个极有能力、极狡猾的恶魔，让一切外部事物和他自己的身体都只是幻象。这种假装是安全的，因为他现在的任务是求知，不是行动。恶魔是对抗习惯的方法，不是他相信的东西；按本站的理解，它没有带来新的怀疑理由。补充（读物外）：别的译本叫 **evil demon** 或 **evil genius**。

points.en: **'I am, I exist' (pp. 4-5):** like Archimedes, he wants just one fixed point. If he convinced himself of anything, he existed; even if a supremely powerful deceiver is deceiving him, he must exist to be deceived, and he cannot be nothing while he thinks he is something. So each time he asserts or conceives "I am, I exist", it is necessarily true (p. 5). It holds while he thinks, not at all times, and it shows that he exists, not yet what he is. Outside the reading: textbooks call this step the cogito; 'I think, therefore I am' is not in this text.
points.zh: “我在，我存在”（第 4–5 页）：像阿基米德一样，他只要一个固定不动的点。只要他说服了自己相信什么，他就存在；就算一个能力至高的骗子在骗他，被骗也需要他存在；只要他在想自己是某个东西，他就不可能什么都不是。所以，每当他说出或心里想到“我在，我存在”，它就必然为真（第 5 页）。它只在他思考时成立，而且只说明他存在，还没说他是什么。补充（读物外）：教科书常把这一步叫“我思”（**the cogito**）；“我思故我在”这句口号不在这份读物里。

points.en: **A thing that thinks (pp. 5-6):** he subtracts from his former picture of himself (a body, and a soul that took nourishment, moved, sensed and thought) everything the deceiver could touch. Nourishment, movement and sensing need a body; only thinking cannot be separated from him. So, strictly speaking, he is only "a thing that thinks" (p. 6): a mind, intelligence, intellect or reason. He leaves open whether this 'I' might be identical with something bodily: the claim is about what he can be certain of, not a proof that mind and body are distinct. Outside the reading: textbooks often call Descartes a dualist; the Second Meditation has not argued for this.
points.zh: 一个思维之物（第 5–6 页）：他从以前的自我形象（一个身体，加上一个会摄取营养、运动、感觉、思考的灵魂）中，减掉骗子能动摇的一切。营养、运动、感觉都需要身体；只有思维和他分不开。所以严格地说，他只是“一个在思考的东西”（第 6 页），也就是心灵、智性、理智或理性。他没有回答这个“我”会不会和某种物体是同一个东西：这是关于他能确定什么的结论，不是证明心灵和身体不同。补充（读物外）：教科书常说笛卡尔是二元论者（**dualism**），第二沉思并没有论证这一点。

points.en: **Imagination and the activities of thinking (pp. 6-7):** imagining is picturing the shape of a bodily thing, so using it to learn what he is would be like falling asleep on purpose to see more clearly in dreams. A thinking thing doubts, understands, affirms, denies, wills, refuses, imagines and senses. Even if he is dreaming, he certainly seems to see light, hear a noise and feel heat, and this cannot be false: in this restricted sense, sensing is thinking.
points.zh: 想象与思维的种种活动（第 6–7 页）：想象（**imagination**）就是描画物体的形状，所以用想象来认识自己，就像为了看得更清楚而故意睡着、指望梦给答案。思维之物会怀疑、理解、肯定、否定、愿意、不愿意、想象、感觉。就算他在做梦，他确实好像看到光、听到声音、感到热，这一点不可能是假的：在这个严格意义上，感觉就是思维。

points.en: **The wax argument (pp. 7-8):** fresh from the honeycomb, the wax has a taste, a smell, a colour, a shape and a size, is hard and cold, and makes a sound when struck; near the fire all of these change, yet it is the same wax. So what he knew in the wax was none of its sensory qualities. What remains is something extended, flexible and changeable; since it can take countless shapes that imagination could never run through, its nature is grasped by the mind alone, through purely mental scrutiny. The argument does not prove that the wax exists.
points.zh: 蜡块论证（**wax argument**，第 7–8 页）：刚从蜂巢里取出的蜡有味道、气味、颜色、形状和大小，又硬又凉，敲一下会出声；放到火边，这些性质全都变了，可它还是同一块蜡。所以他在蜡身上认识到的，不是任何感觉性质。剩下的只是一个有广延、可塑、可变的东西；它能变成想象永远过不完的无数种形状，所以它的本性只由心灵把握，靠的是纯粹心灵的审视（**purely mental scrutiny**）。这个论证没有证明蜡存在。

points.en: **Men in the square (pp. 8-9):** we say we see men crossing the square, but all we see are hats and coats that could conceal automatons; we judge that they are men. So what we call seeing is really a judgment of the mind, and ordinary talk about seeing gives no reason to doubt the result of the wax argument.
points.zh: 广场上的人（第 8–9 页）：我们说看见有人走过广场，其实只看见帽子和外套，里面也可能藏着自动机；“他们是人”是我们判断出来的。所以我们说的“看见”，其实是心灵用判断能力（**faculty of judgment**）做出的判断；日常说的“看见”不能成为怀疑蜡块结论的理由。

points.en: **The mind is better known than the body (p. 9):** if he judges that the wax exists because he sees it, it follows even more evidently that he exists: even if it is not wax, or he has no eyes, he who seems to see must be something; the same holds for touching or imagining the wax and for everything outside him. Bodies, too, are perceived by the intellect, through being understood. So the mind is known more easily and more evidently than the body; 'better known' means more certain and more distinct, not easier to picture.
points.zh: 心灵比物体更容易被认识（第 9 页）：如果他因为看见蜡就判断蜡存在，那就更明显地推出他自己存在：就算那不是蜡、他甚至没有眼睛，正在“好像看见”的他也一定是某个东西；摸到、想象到蜡，以及他以外的一切，都是如此。连物体也是靠理智、靠被理解而被知觉的。所以心灵比物体更容易、更明显地被认识；“更好地被认识”指更确定、更清楚，不是更容易想象。

points.en: **Objections and replies (an interpretation):** (1) if no sure sign tells waking from dreaming, how does he know he has ever dreamt? He needs only that he has no sure sign right now. (2) 'I can doubt that I have a body but not that I think' does not show that he is not a body, and Descartes admits that he does not yet know this (p. 6). (3) We might know it is the same wax by watching it melt; Descartes would reply that watching gives only a series of appearances, and judging that it is one wax is the mind's work.
points.zh: 反驳与回应（本站的理解）：①如果没有标志能区分醒和梦，他怎么知道自己做过梦？他只需要“此刻没有可靠的标志”。②“我能怀疑自己有身体，却不能怀疑自己在思考”推不出“我不是物体”，笛卡尔自己也承认他还不知道（第 6 页）。③也许我们是看着蜡融化，才知道它还是同一块蜡；笛卡尔会回答：看到的只是一连串表象，判断“这是同一块蜡”是心灵的工作。

points.en: **Descartes, Russell and what remains doubtful (an interpretation):** Descartes and Russell (Week 2) both treat habit as an obstacle, but Descartes uses doubt as a tool to reach certainty, while Russell values uncertainty itself. In Week 7 Russell keeps Descartes' method of systematic doubt but says what is certain is a particular experience, not a lasting 'I'. At the end of the Second Meditation, Descartes still does not know whether any body, the wax included, exists; the station has only Meditations 1 and 2.
points.zh: 笛卡尔、罗素与仍然可疑的东西（本站的理解）：笛卡尔和罗素（第 2 周）都把习惯看成障碍，但笛卡尔把怀疑当工具，目的是找到确定的东西；罗素看重的是不确定本身的价值。第 7 周罗素保留笛卡尔的系统怀疑法，但认为确定的只是一个个具体的经验，不是一个持续的“我”。第二沉思结束时，笛卡尔仍不知道任何物体（包括蜡）是否存在；本站只有第一、第二沉思。

formulas.expr:
composite things (physics, astronomy, medicine): doubtful after the dreaming argument
simple and universal things (extension, shape, quantity, place, time): arithmetic and geometry still seem certain
formulas.en: The painter analogy marks where the dreaming doubt stops (Descartes p. 2); the deceiving God goes further.
formulas.zh: 画家类比给梦境怀疑划界（第 2 页）；骗人的上帝走得更远。

formulas.expr:
the wax before the fire → near the fire every sensory quality changes → still the same wax
what remains: something extended, flexible and changeable → grasped by the mind alone
formulas.en: The wax argument (Descartes pp. 7-8); it shows how bodies are known, not that the wax exists.
formulas.zh: 蜡块论证（第 7–8 页）：说明物体怎样被认识，不证明蜡存在。

formulas.expr:
a thinking thing doubts, understands, affirms, denies, wills, refuses, imagines, senses
sensing (restricted sense) = seeming to see, hear, feel heat → cannot be false
formulas.en: Everything on this list belongs to thinking and is as certain as 'I exist' (Descartes pp. 6-7).
formulas.zh: 这些活动都属于思维，和“我存在”一样确定（第 6–7 页）。

points.en: **Russell's question (Ch. 1):** is any knowledge so certain that no reasonable person could doubt it? **Thesis:** what we know immediately are changing **sense-data**; the real table, if it exists, cannot be known directly and has to be inferred from them (Russell pp. 1-3).
points.zh: 罗素（**Bertrand Russell**）的问题（第 1 章）：有没有一种知识确定到任何讲理的人都无法怀疑？论点：我们直接知道的只是会变的感觉材料（**sense-data**）；真实的桌子（如果存在）不能直接知道，只能从感觉材料推出来（罗素第 1–3 页）。

points.en: **Main argument (Ch. 1):** the table's colour changes with the viewpoint, the light (artificial light, darkness) and the viewer (a colour-blind man, blue spectacles); its texture changes under a microscope; its shape changes with perspective. No appearance has a better claim than the others, so, to avoid favouritism, the table in itself has no one real colour, and its real shape is inferred, not seen (pp. 1-3).
points.zh: 主论证（第 1 章）：桌子的颜色随位置、光线（人造光、黑暗）、看的人（色盲、戴蓝色眼镜）而变；质地在显微镜下会变；形状随透视而变。没有哪一种表象比别的更有资格算真的，只挑一种就是偏心（**favouritism**），所以桌子本身没有唯一的真颜色，真正的形状也是推出来的，不是看到的（第 1–3 页）。

points.en: **Russell's question (Ch. 2):** can we know that the table exists when no one perceives it, or might life be one long dream? **Answer:** this cannot be strictly disproved, but independent objects explain our experience more simply, and the belief in them is instinctive and clashes with nothing, so Russell accepts it with a slight doubt from dreams (pp. 6-10).
points.zh: 罗素第 2 章的问题：没人感知时桌子还存在吗？会不会整个人生是一场长梦？回答：这种可能无法被严格驳倒，但“有独立对象”能更简单地解释经验，而且这是一个本能信念，又不和别的信念冲突；所以罗素接受外部世界，只保留一点来自梦的怀疑（第 6–10 页）。

points.en: **Van Inwagen's question:** is there objective truth? **Thesis:** yes. (1) Every belief or assertion says that the World is a certain way, and it is true when the World matches it and false when it does not; (2) the World is, in large part, independent of our beliefs and assertions. So what makes a belief true or false is the thing it is about, not the believer (van Inwagen pp. 1-2).
points.zh: 范·因瓦根（**Peter van Inwagen**）的问题：有没有客观真理（**objective truth**）？论点：有。①每个信念或断言都说世界是某个样子，世界真是那样就为真，不是就为假；②世界在很大程度上独立于我们的信念和断言。所以让信念为真或为假的，是它所关于的对象，不是持有它的人（范·因瓦根第 1–2 页）。

points.en: **Van Inwagen's main arguments:** the geological argument shows that fact F (Mount Everest is 8,849 meters high) would hold in a world that never contained any minds; and anti-Realism seems to refute itself, because it lacks every substitute for truth that it offers. So we should be **Realists** (pp. 5-6, 10-14).
points.zh: 范·因瓦根的主要论证：地质论证说明事实 F（珠峰高 8,849 米）就算从来没有心灵也照样成立；反实在论又显得自我反驳，因为它提出的每个真理替代品，它自己都不具备。所以我们应该做大写的实在论者（**Realists**）（第 5–6、10–14 页）。

points.en: **Appearance vs reality (p. 2):** what things seem to be versus what they are. The painter cares about how things look; the practical man and the philosopher care about what they really are.
points.zh: 表象与实在（**appearance and reality**，第 2 页）：东西看起来怎样 vs 东西本身怎样。画家关心看起来的样子；实用的人和哲学家关心它到底是什么。

points.en: **Four definitions (p. 3):** **sense-data** are what we are immediately aware of in sensation (colours, sounds, smells, hardnesses, roughnesses); a **sensation** is the experience of being aware of them; a **physical object** is a real thing such as the real table (if it exists); **matter** is the collection of all physical objects. Russell's two questions: (1) Does matter exist at all? (2) If it does, what is its nature?
points.zh: 四个定义（第 3 页）：感觉材料（**sense-data**）＝感觉时直接觉察到的东西（颜色、声音、气味、硬度、粗糙度）；感觉（**sensation**）＝对它们的觉察；物理对象（**physical object**）＝真实的东西，比如真实的桌子（如果存在）；物质（**matter**）＝所有物理对象的总和。罗素的两个问题：（1）到底有没有物质？（2）如果有，它的本性是什么？

points.en: **Idealism (pp. 3-5):** Berkeley says the real table is a set of ideas in the mind of God; for Leibniz it is a colony of souls. Both say there is a real table, but that it is mental. Russell rejects the crude idealist argument (anything we can think about exists only as an idea in a mind, so nothing else can exist) as fallacious.
points.zh: 唯心论（**idealism**，第 3–5 页）：贝克莱（**George Berkeley**）说真实的桌子是上帝心中的一组观念；莱布尼茨（**Leibniz**）说它是一群灵魂。两人都承认有真实的桌子，只是说它是心灵的东西。唯心论那个粗糙的论证（凡能被想到的都是某个心灵里的观念，所以别的东西都不能存在），罗素说是谬误的（**fallacious**）。

points.en: **Descartes corrected (pp. 6-7):** Russell keeps Descartes' method of systematic doubt but says 'I think, therefore I am' claims too much. What is certain at once is that "a brown colour is being seen" (p. 7), not that a lasting 'I' sees it; particular thoughts and feelings have primitive certainty, even in dreams.
points.zh: 修正笛卡尔（第 6–7 页）：罗素保留笛卡尔（**René Descartes**）的系统怀疑法，但说“我思故我在”说多了：立刻确定的是“有一块棕色正在被看见”（第 7 页），不是“有一个持续的我在看”。一个个具体的想法和感受有原初的确定性（**primitive certainty**），做梦时也一样。

points.en: **Public objects beg the question (pp. 7-8):** sense-data are private, yet ten people at a dinner-table seem to see the same tablecloth. Arguing from other people's similar sense-data or their testimony assumes that other people exist, but they reach me only through my own sense-data; so the evidence must come from my own private experience.
points.zh: 公共对象的论证窃取论题（**begging the question**，第 7–8 页）：感觉材料是私人的，可十个人围着餐桌，似乎看到同一块桌布。用别人相似的感觉材料或别人的证词来证明公共对象，就预设了别人存在；可别人对我来说也只是我自己的感觉材料。所以证据只能从我自己私人的经验里找。

points.en: **The cat and the dream hypothesis (pp. 8-9):** life as one long dream is not logically impossible. But a cat seen in one part of the room and later in another, and hungry again by the next meal, makes sense only if it exists while unseen, since patches of colour cannot be hungry; people's speech is explained the same way. A banging door can cause a dream of a naval battle: a physical cause, but no matching object.
points.zh: 猫与梦境假说（第 8–9 页）：人生是一场长梦，这在逻辑上并非不可能。可猫一会儿在房间这头、一会儿在那头，到下一顿饭时又饿了，只有假定它没被看见时也存在才讲得通，一块块颜色是不会饿的；别人说话也只能这样解释。关门声能让人梦见海战：有物理的原因，却没有对应的对象。

points.en: **Instinctive belief (pp. 9-10):** we do not argue our way to the external world; we find the belief already in us when we reflect. An instinctive belief may be rejected only if it clashes with others, and all beliefs keep a little doubt. Philosophy's modest job is to rank our instinctive beliefs and fit them into a harmonious system.
points.zh: 本能信念（**instinctive belief**，第 9–10 页）：外部世界不是论证出来的，一反思就发现这个信念已经在心里。只有和别的信念冲突，才可以抛弃一个本能信念；所有信念都保留一点怀疑。哲学的任务比较谦虚：给本能信念排出层级，整理成一个和谐的体系。

points.en: **Not dogmatism, not 'true for me' (pp. 1-3):** believing that every claim is objectively true or false does not make Mary the judge of which ones are true: no one today can settle whether other planets have intelligent life, yet that claim is true or false. Truth is one: 'true for me' just means 'what I think'. Qualifications: a meaningless sentence (perhaps Royce's) is neither true nor false, and vague words ('tall') make some claims indeterminate, which is itself an objective status.
points.zh: 不是独断，也没有“对我为真”（第 1–3 页）：相信每句话都客观地非真即假，不等于 Mary 自封真理的裁判：别的星球上有没有智慧生命，今天没人能断定，但这句话照样有真假。真理只有一个：“对我为真”只是“我这么想”。两个限定：无意义的话（也许 Royce 的那句）无所谓真假；模糊的词（“高”）会让有些说法不确定（**indeterminate**），而“不确定”本身也是一种客观状态。

points.en: **realism vs Realism (pp. 4-5):** lowercase **realism** opposes **idealism** (is everything that exists mental?); capital-R **Realism** opposes **anti-Realism** (is there objective truth, or does the way the World is depend on minds?). 'Mind-independent' means different things in the two debates: the idealist says everything is mental, yet holds that the way the World is does not depend on minds, so an idealist can be a Realist.
points.zh: 小写 realism 与大写 Realism（第 4–5 页）：小写的实在论（**realism**）对唯心论（**idealism**），问一切存在的东西是不是都是心灵的；大写的实在论（**Realism**）对反实在论（**anti-Realism**），问有没有客观真理、世界的样子是不是由心灵决定。两场争论里“独立于心灵”意思不同：唯心论者说万物的本性是心灵的，但认为世界是什么样并不依赖心灵，所以唯心论者也可以是大写的实在论者。

points.en: **Objection and reply on Everest (pp. 5-6):** the geological argument says the plate collision that raised the Himalayas would have gone exactly the same with no intelligent beings, and geologists already explain unobserved processes; it presupposes that idealism is false. Objection: you cannot imagine an event with no one watching (compare imagining your own funeral). Reply: the argument needs only that we understand descriptions, not that we form images; and one can paint someone who is alone.
points.zh: 珠峰的反驳与回应（第 5–6 页）：地质论证说，就算从来没有智慧生命，把喜马拉雅山挤起来的板块碰撞也会完全一样地发生，地质学家本来就在解释没人看见的过程；这个论证预设唯心论为假。反驳：你没法想象一件没人在看的事（就像没法想象自己的葬礼）。回应：论证只需要我们理解描述，不需要在脑中成像；何况画一个独处的人也完全可以。

points.en: **Social construct and schmeight (pp. 6-10):** the anti-Realist says mountain boundaries (set by bodies like the International Geographical Union) and 'height' are conventions, so F depends on minds. Reply: conventions only decide which object the name 'Mount Everest' picks out (x rather than y) and which property the word 'height' names; they do not change how high x is. With another benchmark we would have 'schmeight', so 'Everest is 8,849 meters high' and 'Everest is 8,773 meters schmigh' can both be true.
points.zh: 社会建构与 schmeight（第 6–10 页）：反实在论者说，山的边界（由国际地理联合会之类的机构划定）和“高度”都是约定，所以 F 依赖心灵。回应：约定只决定“Mount Everest”这个名字指哪个对象（x 而不是 y）、height 这个词指哪个性质，不改变 x 有多高。换一个基准，就得到另一个性质 schmeight，所以“珠峰高 8,849 米”和“珠峰 schmigh 8,773 米”可以同时为真。

points.en: **AR refutes itself (pp. 10-14):** AR says there is no objective truth or falsity, so AR needs a substitute 'good' status. 'Fitting in with our experience' fails: rejecting 'Lions are carnivorous' could get you eaten, but rejecting AR gets no one into trouble. A private substitute ('fits my experience') would mean Andrew and Rachel do not really disagree; a public one must (a) belong to the clearly good statements and not the clearly bad ones and (b) belong to anti-Realism itself, and every proposal so far seems to fail (b).
points.zh: AR 自我反驳（第 10–14 页）：AR 说没有客观的真和假，于是 AR 需要一个替代的“好”状态。“符合我们的经验”不行：不信“狮子吃肉”可能被吃掉，不信 AR 却不会让任何人碰壁。私人的替代品（符合“我的”经验）会让 Andrew 和 Rachel 其实没有分歧；公共的替代品必须（a）公认的好陈述有、坏陈述没有，（b）反实在论自己也有，而到目前为止的每个提案看来都过不了（b）。

points.en: **Comparing the two readings (an interpretation, not either author's words):** Russell asks whether matter exists and what it is (realism vs idealism, plus a doubt about knowledge); van Inwagen asks whether there is objective truth (Realism vs anti-Realism). Russell's admission that the external world cannot be proved concerns knowledge, so it does not make him an anti-Realist. Both argue from explanation: Russell's cat, van Inwagen's geology.
points.zh: 两篇对比（本站的理解，不是两位作者的原话）：罗素问有没有物质、它是什么（小写实在论对唯心论，再加上对知识的怀疑）；范·因瓦根问有没有客观真理（大写实在论对反实在论）。罗素承认证明不了外部世界，这是关于“知道”的问题，不会让他变成反实在论者。两人都从解释出发：罗素的猫，范·因瓦根的地质学。

formulas.expr:
Ch. 2: dream hypothesis (logically possible) vs independent objects (simpler, instinctive, no clash)
→ accept the external world, with a slight doubt from dreams
formulas.en: Russell does not prove the external world exists; he prefers the simpler, instinctive hypothesis (Russell pp. 8-10).
formulas.zh: 罗素没有证明外部世界存在：两个假说逻辑上都可能，他选更简单、又是本能信念的那个，并保留一点怀疑（罗素第 8–10 页）。

formulas.expr:
Geological argument: F = Mount Everest is 8,849 m high
F would hold with no minds at all → F is mind-independent → Realism
formulas.en: The argument presupposes that idealism is false and needs only that we understand descriptions of unobserved events (van Inwagen pp. 5-6).
formulas.zh: 这个论证预设唯心论为假；它只要求我们理解对没人观察的过程的描述，不要求想象出画面（范·因瓦根第 5–6 页）。

formulas.expr:
realism ↔ idealism (is everything mental?)
Realism ↔ anti-Realism (is there objective truth?)
formulas.en: Keep the capital R: an idealist can still be a Realist (van Inwagen pp. 4-5).
formulas.zh: 大小写别混：小写对唯心论，大写对反实在论；唯心论者仍可以是大写的实在论者（范·因瓦根第 4–5 页）。

points.en: **Hume's question (pp. 1-2):** what evidence assures us of matters of fact that go beyond what our senses and memory now present? **Thesis:** all such reasoning rests on cause and effect, causes are known only by experience, and conclusions from experience rest on no reasoning at all but on **custom** (Hume, Enquiry pp. 1-12).
points.zh: 休谟（**David Hume**）的问题（第 1–2 页）：超出眼前感官和记忆的实际的事情，我们凭什么证据相信？论点：这类推理都靠因果关系；因果只能从经验知道；而从经验得出的结论根本不靠推理，靠的是习惯（**custom**）（休谟《人类理解研究》第 1–12 页）。

points.en: **Relations of ideas vs matters of fact (p. 1):** relations of ideas (geometry, algebra, arithmetic, such as 'three times five is half of thirty') are certain by intuition or demonstration and are found by thought alone; denying one is a contradiction. The contrary of a matter of fact is always possible and just as clearly conceivable ('the sun will not rise tomorrow'), so no matter of fact can be demonstrated.
points.zh: 观念的关系 vs 实际的事情（第 1 页）：观念的关系（几何、代数、算术，比如“三乘五等于三十的一半”）靠直观或证明就能确定，单凭思考就能发现，否定它就矛盾。实际的事情的反面永远可能、也同样能清楚设想（“明天太阳不会升起”），所以实际的事情都不能被证明。

points.en: **Main argument (pp. 7, 9):** all reasoning is either demonstrative (relations of ideas) or moral, that is probable (matters of fact). Demonstration cannot show that the future will resemble the past, because a change in the course of nature implies no contradiction (snow that tastes of salt, trees that flourish in December). Probable reasoning cannot show it either, because it rests on cause and effect and experience, which already assume it, so the argument would go in a circle.
points.zh: 主论证（第 7、9 页）：推理只有两种：证明推理（关于观念的关系）和道德推理，也就是或然推理（关于实际的事情）。证明推理证明不了“未来会像过去”，因为自然进程改变并不矛盾（像雪却尝起来是咸的、树在十二月开花，都想得出来）。或然推理也证明不了，因为它靠因果和经验，而这些本身就预设了“未来像过去”，用它来证明就是兜圈子。

points.en: **Sceptical solution (pp. 10-13):** since no argument takes the step from past to future, something just as strong must: **custom or habit**, the tendency that repetition creates to do the same again without reasoning. "Custom, then, is the great guide of human life" (p. 12); without it we would know nothing beyond memory and the senses.
points.zh: 怀疑论式的解决（**sceptical solution**，第 10–13 页）：既然没有论证带我们从过去走到将来，就一定有同样有力的别的原则：习惯（**custom or habit**），即重复产生的、不经推理就再做一次的倾向。“习惯是人生的伟大向导”（第 12 页）；没有它，我们除了记忆和感官之外什么事实都不知道。

points.en: **Goodman's question (pp. 1-4):** which hypotheses are confirmed by their instances? **Thesis:** confirmation depends on more than syntactical form; only lawlike hypotheses are confirmed by their instances, and so far nothing tells us what makes a hypothesis lawlike. He calls this the **new riddle of induction** (p. 4).
points.zh: 古德曼（**Nelson Goodman**）的问题（第 1–4 页）：哪些假说能被它们的实例确证（**confirmation**）？论点：确证不只看句法形式；只有似律的假说能被实例确证，可到目前为止，没有任何东西告诉我们什么让一个假说成为似律的。他把这个问题叫作归纳的新谜题（**new riddle of induction**，第 4 页）。

points.en: **Grue argument (pp. 1-2):** suppose every emerald examined before time t is green. Each report confirms 'All emeralds are green', but every emerald examined so far is also **grue**, so the parallel reports equally confirm 'All emeralds are grue'. The two predict different colours for emeralds examined after t (a grue one would be blue). So a purely formal definition of confirmation supports incompatible predictions: "anything confirms anything" (p. 2).
points.zh: grue 论证（第 1–2 页）：设 t 之前检查过的祖母绿都是绿的。每条报告都确证“所有祖母绿都是绿的”；可目前检查过的每颗祖母绿也都是 grue 的，对应的报告同样确证“所有祖母绿都是 grue 的”。两个假说对 t 之后检查的祖母绿预测的颜色不同（grue 的那颗会是蓝的）。所以只看形式的确证定义会同等支持互相冲突的预测：“anything confirms anything”（第 2 页）。

points.en: **Cause and effect (p. 2):** reasoning about absent facts always runs through cause and effect: a letter tells you your friend is in France; a watch found on a desert island tells you people were once there. Without such a connection the inference would be groundless.
points.zh: 因果关系（**cause and effect**，第 2 页）：关于不在眼前的事实的推理，都要经过因果：一封信让你知道朋友在法国；荒岛上捡到一块表，让你知道那里曾经有人。没有这种联系，推论就毫无根据。

points.en: **Not a priori (pp. 2-5):** Adam, with perfect reason but no experience, could not tell from water's fluidity and transparency that it would suffocate him. An effect is a separate event from its cause, so any effect we invent a priori is arbitrary: both billiard balls might as well stay at rest, or the first bounce back. Causes are learned only from experience of **constant conjunction**.
points.zh: 因果不是先验的（**a priori**，第 2–5 页）：亚当理性完美却没有经验，看不出透明流动的水会让他窒息。结果和原因是两件不同的事，所以先验编出来的结果都是任意的：两个台球也可以都一动不动，第一个也可以弹回来。因果只能从恒常结合（**constant conjunction**）的经验中学到。

points.en: **Sensible qualities vs secret powers (pp. 5-7):** experience shows us bread's colour, weight and consistency, never the secret power that nourishes us. We always move from 'this has always been followed by that' to 'similar things will be followed by similar effects', but the step is not intuitive; if it were reasoning, it would need a connecting **medium**, and no one can produce one.
points.zh: 可感性质与隐秘力量（第 5–7 页）：经验让我们看到面包的颜色、重量、软硬，却从来看不到让它养人的隐秘力量（**secret powers**）。我们总是从“这一直伴随着那个”走到“相似的东西将来也会伴随相似的结果”，但这一步不是直观的；如果它是推理，就需要一个中介（**medium**），可谁也拿不出来。

points.en: **Eggs, and the child and the candle (pp. 8-10):** eggs look exactly alike, yet we expect the same taste only after long uniform experience, whereas reasoning would conclude the same from one instance as from a hundred. A child burnt by a candle flame avoids candles; if an argument produced this, it would be simple enough for an infant, and no one can state it.
points.zh: 鸡蛋，以及孩子和蜡烛（第 8–10 页）：鸡蛋长得一模一样，可我们要经过长期一贯的经验才会期待它们味道相同；而推理从一个例子和从一百个例子得出的结论应该一样。被蜡烛烫过的孩子会躲开蜡烛；如果这是论证带来的，论证就得简单到婴儿都懂，可谁也说不出来。

points.en: **Objection and reply (p. 9):** 'Your practice refutes your doubts: you still eat bread.' Hume replies that as an agent he is quite satisfied; as a philosopher he only asks what the inference rests on. He never says we should stop trusting experience, and his conclusion is about where the inference comes from, not that it is false.
points.zh: 反驳与回应（第 9 页）：“你照样吃面包，你的行动就驳倒了你的怀疑。”休谟回答：作为行动者，他完全满意；作为哲学家，他只是追问这个推论的根据。他从没说不该相信经验；他的结论说的是推论从哪里来，不是说推论是错的。

points.en: **Belief (Section 5, Part II, pp. 14-16):** we can picture a man's head on a horse's body but cannot believe such an animal existed, so belief is not an extra idea added at will. It differs from fiction only in how it feels: a livelier, firmer and steadier way of conceiving the same content (p. 15). Ideas are linked by three principles of association: resemblance, contiguity and causation.
points.zh: 信念（第 5 节第二部分，第 14–16 页）：我们能想象人头配马身，却没法相信真有这种动物，所以信念不是随意加上的额外观念。它和虚构的区别只在感受：同一个内容，被更生动、更牢固、更稳定地构想（第 15 页）。观念之间靠三条联想原则相连：相似、接近、因果。

points.en: **Copper and third sons (p. 1):** a piece of copper that conducts electricity makes it more credible that other copper does, so it confirms 'All copper conducts electricity'; a man in this room who is a third son does not confirm 'All men now in this room are third sons'. Both hypotheses generalize their evidence in the same way, so the difference is not in their form: the first is **lawlike**, the second **accidental**, and lawlikeness does not depend on truth.
points.zh: 铜与第三子（第 1 页）：一块导电的铜让“别的铜也导电”更可信，所以它确证“所有铜都导电”；房间里一个男人是第三子，却不确证“房间里所有男人都是第三子”。两个假说概括证据的方式一样，所以区别不在形式：前者是似律的（**lawlike**），后者是偶然的（**accidental**）；似律与否和真假无关。

points.en: **Four failed fixes (pp. 2-4):** (1) 'smuggled information' (as with the paradox of the ravens): stating it openly changes nothing under the definition; (2) indirect support from related hypotheses: iron supports zirconium but not 'the objects on my desk', and the important difference comes down to H being lawlike while K is not, so the fix is circular; (3) complete generality: 'All emeralds are grue' contains no term for a particular thing, any such term can be replaced by a coined predicate, and banning hypotheses equivalent to ones with such terms excludes either nothing or everything, depending on how the ban is read ('All grass is green' is equivalent to 'All grass in London or elsewhere is green'); (4) purely qualitative predicates: qualitativeness is relative (see bleen).
points.zh: 四个失败的补救（第 2–4 页）：（1）“偷运信息”（像乌鸦悖论那样）：把信息明说出来，定义的判断也不变；（2）相关假说的间接支持：铁的证据支持锆，却不支持“我桌上的东西”，关键区别说到底是 H 似律而 K 不是，所以这个补救是循环的；（3）完全普遍性：“所有祖母绿都是 grue 的”里本来就没有指称特定事物的词，这种词也总能换成自造的谓词；再把“等价于含这种词的假说”也一起禁止，看怎么理解，结果要么什么都排除不了，要么什么都排除了（“所有草都是绿的”等价于“伦敦或别处的所有草都是绿的”）；（4）纯质谓词：纯质是相对的（见 bleen）。

points.en: **Bleen and symmetry (pp. 3-4):** an emerald is **bleen** if it is examined before t and blue, or not examined before t and green. Objection: green and blue are purely qualitative, while grue and bleen mention a time. Reply: starting from grue and bleen, green needs a time too (green = examined before t and grue, or not examined before t and bleen), so qualitativeness depends on where you start. Goodman still agrees that green and blue are the well-behaved predicates.
points.zh: bleen 与对称性（第 3–4 页）：一颗祖母绿是 bleen 的：在 t 之前被检查过并且是蓝的，或者没在 t 之前被检查过并且是绿的。反驳：green、blue 是纯质的，grue、bleen 提到了时间。回应：从 grue、bleen 出发，green 也要用时间来定义（green＝t 之前检查且 grue，或没在 t 之前检查且 bleen），所以纯质不纯质取决于从哪里出发。古德曼仍然同意 green、blue 是表现良好的谓词。

points.en: **'Why worry about grue?' (p. 4):** we are unlikely ever to predict with grue, so is a definition that works for normal hypotheses not enough? Goodman: true only in the way that daily life also gets by without any theory of induction; if we want a theory, we cannot excuse its gross anomalies by avoiding them in practice. Odd cases, like textbook cases of a disease, show a widespread illness most clearly. The excerpt ends with no answer and no clue.
points.zh: “干嘛在乎 grue？”（第 4 页）：我们不太会用 grue 做预测，定义对正常的假说管用不就够了？古德曼：照这个说法，日常生活也用不着任何归纳理论；只要想要一个理论，就不能用“实际中能避开”来为它的严重反常开脱。怪例子就像教科书里的典型病例，最清楚地显示出普遍的毛病。节选到最后没有答案，连线索也没有。

points.en: **Hume vs Goodman (our interpretation; the excerpt never mentions Hume):** Hume asks what entitles any step from observed to unobserved cases; Goodman asks which hypotheses their instances confirm. Hume ends with custom; Goodman's excerpt ends with an open riddle. One link: Hume's principle that the future resembles the past does not say in which respect, and past emeralds are uniformly green and uniformly grue.
points.zh: 休谟与古德曼（本站的理解；节选里根本没提休谟）：休谟问从观察过的情况推到没观察过的情况凭什么；古德曼问哪些假说能被实例确证。休谟以习惯收尾，古德曼的节选以没解开的谜题收尾。一个联系：休谟的“未来会像过去”没说在哪方面像，而过去的祖母绿既一贯是绿的，也一贯是 grue 的。

points.en: **Outside the reading (labels you may hear):** 'Hume's fork' (relations of ideas vs matters of fact), 'the problem of induction' (the syllabus title for this week) and 'the uniformity of nature' (Hume's assumption that the future will resemble the past) are later labels. Hume's text uses none of them, so give his own wording too.
points.zh: 补充（读物外）：“休谟之叉”（**Hume's fork**，指观念的关系和实际的事情的二分）、“归纳问题”（**the problem of induction**，课程大纲给这一周起的标题）、“自然齐一性”（**the uniformity of nature**，指休谟说的“未来会像过去”这个预设）都是后人的叫法，休谟原文一个都没用；答题用这些标签时，最好同时写出休谟自己的说法。

formulas.expr:
matter of fact beyond senses and memory ← cause and effect ← experience (constant conjunction) ← ?
no reasoning fills the last step → custom or habit
formulas.en: Hume's chain of questions: each answer raises the next, and the last step is made by custom, not by reasoning (Hume pp. 2-12).
formulas.zh: 休谟的一串追问：事实推理靠因果，因果靠经验，从经验得出的结论又靠什么？没有推理能补上这一步，补上它的是习惯（第 2–12 页）。

formulas.expr: green (emeralds) = examined before t and grue, OR not examined before t and bleen
formulas.en: Goodman's symmetry: starting from grue and bleen, green and blue need a time term, so qualitativeness is relative (Goodman p. 4).
formulas.zh: 古德曼的对称性：从 grue、bleen 出发，green、blue 反而要带时间词，所以“纯质”是相对的（古德曼第 4 页）。

formulas.expr:
(1) smuggled information → declaring it changes nothing
(2) indirect support (H vs K) → circular
(3) complete generality → excludes nothing or everything
(4) purely qualitative predicates → qualitativeness is relative
formulas.en: All four fixes fail, so there is still no criterion of lawlikeness: the new riddle of induction (Goodman pp. 2-4).
formulas.zh: 四个补救都失败，所以目前还没有判断似律的标准：这就是归纳的新谜题（古德曼第 2–4 页）。

points.en: **Nagel's question:** can consciousness be explained by physical reduction? Consciousness is the reason the mind-body problem is so hard (p. 2). **Thesis:** no current physical or functional account captures the **subjective character of experience**, because it is tied to a point of view; physicalism may be true, but at present we cannot understand how (pp. 3-4, 12-13).
points.zh: 内格尔（**Thomas Nagel**）的问题：意识能用物理还原（**reduction**）来解释吗？正是意识让身心问题这么难（第 2 页）。论点：现有的物理或功能说明，都抓不住经验的主观特征（**subjective character of experience**），因为它连着一个观点；物理主义（**physicalism**）也许为真，但我们现在不理解它怎么可能为真（第 3–4、12–13 页）。

points.en: **Nagel's criterion (p. 3):** a creature is conscious just in case "there is something that it is like to be that organism", that is, something it is like for the creature itself. Nagel calls this the subjective character of experience, and it has nothing to do with behaviour, language or intelligence.
points.zh: 内格尔的标准（第 3 页）：一个生物有意识，当且仅当“成为这个生物是有某种样子的”，而且是对它自己而言的样子。这就是经验的主观特征；它不看行为、语言，也不看聪不聪明。

points.en: **Main argument (pp. 9-12):** successful reductions (lightning, sound as a wave) become more objective by leaving a species' point of view behind; this works because the thing studied is external to that viewpoint. Experience is not external to its point of view, so each step toward objectivity takes us farther from its real nature. So the usual appearance-to-reality model of reduction cannot be applied to experience.
points.zh: 主论证（第 9–12 页）：成功的还原（闪电、声音其实是波）靠离开某个物种的观点变得更客观；这行得通，是因为被研究的东西外在于那个观点。可经验并不外在于它的观点，所以每往客观走一步，就离它的真实本性更远一步。因此“从表象走向实在”的通常还原模式用不到经验上。

points.en: **Chalmers's question:** 'Will I survive uploading?' splits into two: will the upload be conscious, and will it be me? **Thesis:** an upload that is a functional isomorph of my brain would very probably be conscious (the gradual uploading argument), and more generally consciousness is an organizational invariant; but that does not settle whether the upload would be me (Chalmers pp. 1-6).
points.zh: 查默斯（**David Chalmers**）的问题：“我能在上传中存活吗”分成两个：上传体会有意识吗？它会是我吗？论点：作为我大脑功能同构体（**functional isomorph**）的上传体很可能有意识（逐步上传论证），更一般地说，意识是组织不变量（**organizational invariant**）；但这回答不了上传体是不是我（查默斯第 1–6 页）。

points.en: **Main argument (gradual uploading, pp. 3-5):** replace the brain one component at a time with computational duplicates, so behaviour and reports never change. Consciousness must then disappear suddenly, fade gradually, or stay. Sudden disappearance would mean all consciousness vanishing when one tiny part is replaced; fading would mean badly degraded experience while the system behaves and believes exactly as before. Both are implausible, so consciousness most plausibly stays, and full uploads are conscious.
points.zh: 主论证（逐步上传，第 3–5 页）：把大脑一次换掉一个部件，换成计算复制品，行为和报告始终不变。那么意识要么突然消失，要么逐渐褪色，要么一直都在。突然消失意味着换掉一个极小的部件，全部意识就没了；逐渐褪色意味着经验严重退化，行为和信念却和原来完全一样。两者都不可信，所以最可信的是意识一直都在，完整的上传体也有意识。

points.en: **Robots (pp. 3-4):** functional, intentional and causal-role analyses of the mind could all be true of robots that act like people but experience nothing, so they leave subjective character out. Nagel grants that mental states have causes, effects and functions; he denies that these are the whole story.
points.zh: 机器人（第 3–4 页）：对心灵的功能分析、意向分析、因果角色分析，对行为像人、却什么也体验不到的机器人同样成立，所以它们漏掉了主观特征。内格尔承认心灵状态有原因、结果和功能，只否认这些就是全部。

points.en: **The bat (pp. 5-7):** bats are mammals, so they surely have experience, but they perceive mainly by sonar, unlike any human sense. Imagining webbed arms, catching insects at dusk and hanging upside down shows only how it would feel for me to act like a bat, not how being a bat is for the bat itself. We get only a **schematic conception**; the same gap exists between people (someone deaf and blind from birth).
points.zh: 蝙蝠（第 5–7 页）：蝙蝠是哺乳动物，肯定有经验，但它主要靠声呐，也就是回声定位（**echolocation**）来感知，和人类任何感官都不同。想象手臂有蹼、黄昏时捕虫、倒挂着睡觉，只能告诉我“我”像蝙蝠那样行动会怎样，不能告诉我做蝙蝠对蝙蝠自己来说是什么样子。我们只能有一个粗略的概念（**schematic conception**）；人和人之间也有这种鸿沟（天生又聋又盲的人）。

points.en: **Facts beyond our concepts (pp. 7-9):** intelligent bats or Martians would be wrong to conclude that being human is not like anything specific, and transfinite numbers would have existed even if everyone had died before Cantor. So Nagel is a realist about subjective facts. A point of view is a type that similar beings share, not something private to one person.
points.zh: 超出人类概念的事实（第 7–9 页）：有智慧的蝙蝠或火星人如果断定“做人类没有什么确切的样子”，那就错了；就算所有人在康托尔之前都死了，超穷数也照样存在。所以内格尔对主观事实是实在论者。观点（**point of view**）是足够相似的生物共享的一种类型，不是某个人私有的。

points.en: **Lightning and the Martian (p. 10):** a Martian scientist could understand lightning physically without our visual concepts, because lightning is external to our point of view.
