This is a contrast case, not Nagel's argument against reduction: objectivity is a direction understanding can travel, and experience cannot be left behind in the same way.
points.zh: 闪电与火星人（第 10 页）：火星科学家不懂我们的视觉概念，也能从物理上理解闪电，因为闪电外在于我们的观点。这是一个对照，不是内格尔反对还原的论证：客观性是理解可以前进的一个方向，而经验没法像闪电那样把观点留在身后。

points.en: **Physicalism not yet understood (pp. 13-15):** Nagel does not conclude that physicalism is false. To understand 'X is Y' we need a theory showing how both terms can pick out one thing; without it, physicalism is like a pre-Socratic philosopher saying that matter is energy. We can even have evidence for something we do not understand: the caterpillar locked in a safe, and the butterfly found there weeks later.
points.zh: 物理主义：还理解不了（第 13–15 页）：内格尔没有得出“物理主义是错的”。要理解“X 就是 Y”，需要一套理论说明两个词怎么能指向同一个东西；没有它，物理主义就像一位前苏格拉底哲学家说“物质就是能量”。我们甚至可以对自己不理解的事有证据：锁进保险箱的毛毛虫，几周后箱里是一只蝴蝶。

points.en: **Objective phenomenology (pp. 16-17):** Nagel proposes new concepts that could describe at least part of what an experience is like to beings who cannot have it, for example explaining sight to someone blind from birth; loose cross-sense comparisons, such as likening red to a trumpet's sound, are of little use. Nagel doubts that we can seriously consider any physical theory of mind before we have thought more about subjective and objective.
points.zh: 客观现象学（**objective phenomenology**，第 16–17 页）：内格尔提议发展新概念，向不能有某种经验的生物至少描述它的一部分，比如向天生的盲人解释“看见”；“红色像小号声”这类松散的类比用处不大。内格尔认为，在多想想主观与客观之前，我们恐怕还没法认真考虑任何物理的心灵理论。

points.en: **Why it matters and why it is hard (Chalmers pp. 1-2):** conscious experience is a central part of what gives life meaning and value, so an unconscious upload would be at best a zombified existence. Consciousness is a **further fact**: complete physical knowledge does not settle it (Mary knows all the physics of colour vision but not what seeing red is like; a full physical description of a mouse leaves open what it is like to be one), and there is no consciousness meter.
points.zh: 为什么重要、为什么难（查默斯第 1–2 页）：有意识的经验给了生活很大一部分意义和价值，没有意识的上传体最多是一种僵尸化的存在。意识是一个进一步的事实（**further fact**）：完整的物理知识定不下它（玛丽知道颜色视觉的全部物理过程，却不知道看见红色是什么样子；对老鼠的完整物理描述，也说不出做老鼠是什么样子），而且我们没有“意识计”。

points.en: **Biological vs functionalist theories (pp. 2-3):** biological theories, favoured by Block and Searle, say only biological systems can be conscious; functionalist theories, favoured by Dennett and Chalmers himself, say what matters is causal organization. We have no idea how silicon could be conscious, but no idea how neurons could be either; with no known principled difference between them, the default is that both kinds of system can be conscious.
points.zh: 生物论 vs 功能论（第 2–3 页）：生物论（**Block**、**Searle** 同情它）说只有生物系统能有意识；功能论（**Dennett** 和查默斯同情它）说要紧的是因果组织。我们不知道硅怎么会有意识，可同样不知道神经元怎么会有意识；既然不知道两者有原则性的差别，默认态度就是两种系统都能有意识。

points.en: **Functional isomorph (p. 3):** a perfect upload whose every component duplicates the input/output behaviour of the matching part of the brain, so that its processing mirrors the brain's step by step. That such isomorphs are possible is an assumption (cognition must be computable), not a conclusion.
points.zh: 功能同构体（**functional isomorph**，第 3 页）：完美的上传体，它的每个部件都复制大脑对应部件的输入／输出行为，处理过程一步步对应大脑。“功能同构体是可能的”是一个假定（认知必须可计算），不是结论。

points.en: **Organizational invariance (pp. 5-6):** Chalmers argues that a system's conscious states depend only on how its parts are causally organized, not on what they are made of, so a silicon system organized exactly like a brain has the same conscious states as that brain. A simulated rainstorm does not make anything wet, but a simulated computer really is a computer; consciousness is like being a computer, so a good enough simulation of a conscious brain would itself be conscious.
points.zh: 组织不变量（**organizational invariant**，第 5–6 页）：查默斯论证，一个系统有什么意识状态，只取决于它各部分的因果组织方式，不取决于它们是什么做的；所以和大脑组织得完全一样的硅系统，意识状态也和那个大脑一样。模拟的暴雨不会让任何东西变湿，模拟的计算机却是计算机；意识属于后一类，所以对有意识大脑足够好的模拟，自己也会有意识。

points.en: **Personal identity (p. 6):** on the optimistic view, the upload and the original are one and the same person; on the pessimistic view they are two different people. For destructive uploading this is life or death: survival, or death plus a simulacrum in your place. Organizational invariance does not help here, and the excerpt breaks off before Chalmers gives his own answer.
points.zh: 人格同一性（**personal identity**，第 6 页）：乐观观点认为上传体和原来的人是同一个人；悲观观点认为不是。对破坏性上传（**destructive uploading**）来说，这是生死问题：要么是存活，要么是死亡外加一个顶替的仿制品。诉诸组织不变量在这里帮不上忙；节选在查默斯给出自己的答案之前就断了。

points.en: **Nagel and Chalmers compared (an interpretation):** both define consciousness as there being something it is like to be a creature, and both say physical description alone leaves out what experience is like (the bat; Mary and the mouse). But they ask different questions: Nagel asks whether physicalism can be understood; Chalmers asks which systems are conscious. Chalmers's functionalism is about the physical correlates of consciousness, not the functional analysis of what consciousness is that Nagel attacks.
points.zh: 内格尔与查默斯对比（本站的理解）：两人都把意识定义为“成为某个生物是有某种样子的”，也都认为单靠物理描述说不出经验是什么样子（蝙蝠；玛丽和老鼠）。但问题不同：内格尔问物理主义能不能被理解；查默斯问哪些系统有意识。查默斯的功能论讲的是意识的物理关联物，不是内格尔批评的“用功能分析意识是什么”。

formulas.expr:
Reduction: appearance → reality by leaving our viewpoint behind (lightning, sound)
Experience: its viewpoint is essential → more objective = farther away
formulas.en: Why Nagel thinks the usual model of reduction cannot reach experience (Nagel pp. 10-12).
formulas.zh: 内格尔认为通常的还原模式够不着经验的原因（第 10–12 页）。

formulas.expr:
Neurons: no idea how they are conscious = Silicon: no idea how it is conscious
no known principled difference → default: both can be conscious
formulas.en: Chalmers's case against assuming that only biology can be conscious; it sets a default, not a proof (Chalmers pp. 2-3).
formulas.zh: 查默斯的论证：不该默认只有生物能有意识；它只确立默认态度，不是证明（查默斯第 2–3 页）。

formulas.expr:
Organizational invariant: same causal organization → same conscious states (any substrate)
simulated rainstorm: not wet | simulated computer: a computer
formulas.en: If consciousness is like being a computer, not like being wet, a good enough simulation of a conscious brain is conscious (Chalmers p. 6).
formulas.zh: 意识像“是计算机”而不像“湿”，所以足够好的模拟会有意识（查默斯第 6 页）。

formulas.expr:
Will I survive uploading?
= Will the upload be conscious? + Will the upload be me?
formulas.en: A yes to the first question does not give a yes to the second (Chalmers pp. 1, 6).
formulas.zh: 第一个问题答“是”，不等于第二个问题也答“是”（查默斯第 1、6 页）。

points.en: **Chalmers's question (pp. 1-2):** who or what is on the other side when we chat with an LLM, and what does a name like 'Aura' refer to? An **LLM interlocutor** is the apparent entity a user interacts with. **Thesis:** against Birch's persistent interlocutor illusion, there often really is a persistent interlocutor: a **virtual instance** of the model (one model) or a **thread** (several models).
points.zh: 查默斯（**David Chalmers**）的问题（第 1–2 页）：和大语言模型（LLM）说话时，我们在和谁（或什么）说话？“Aura”这样的名字指的是什么？LLM 对话者（**LLM interlocutor**）＝用户看起来在与之互动的那个实体。论点：伯奇（**Jonathan Birch**）说这是“持续对话者错觉”；查默斯反对：很多时候确实有一个持续的对话者，在单一模型时是模型的虚拟实例（**virtual instance**），模型会换时是一条线程（**thread**）。

points.en: **Main argument (by elimination, pp. 8-16):** an interlocutor should be interactive, persistent, coherent, faithful and unified. The model fails (abstract, unchanging, and it would be both Aura and Beta); a hardware instance fails (distributed serving makes it fragmented; multi-tenancy makes it incoherent or faithless). A virtual instance or a thread meets the requirements, so that is the interlocutor.
points.zh: 主论证（排除法，第 8–16 页）：对话者应该是交互的、持续的、连贯的、忠实的、统一的。模型不行（抽象、不变、会既是 Aura 又是 Beta）；硬件实例也不行（分布式服务让它碎片化，多租户让它不连贯或不忠实）。虚拟实例或线程满足这些条件，所以对话者就是它们。

points.en: **Quasi-belief (pp. 4-5):** a system quasi-believes p when its behavior can be interpreted, under a suitable scheme, as believing p; quasi-desire likewise. Chalmers offers this as a stipulative definition, not a theory of belief. 'Quasi' means apparent or seeming, not almost, so it leaves open whether quasi-beliefs are real beliefs.
points.zh: 准信念（**quasi-belief**，第 4–5 页）：在合适的解释方案下，一个系统的行为可以被解释为相信 p，它就“准相信”p；准欲望同理。查默斯把这当作约定性定义，不是关于“信念是什么”的理论。“准”的意思是看起来的、似乎的，不是“差一点的”，所以它不回答准信念是不是真正的信念。

points.en: **Why not start from consciousness or belief (pp. 3-4):** no one knows whether LLMs are conscious; most theorists deny it, for reasons that are not conclusive. Whether they have genuine beliefs and desires is also contested; interpretivism would grant them, but most philosophers reject it. So Chalmers needs a neutral starting point: quasi-interpretivism.
points.zh: 为什么不从意识或信念出发（第 3–4 页）：LLM 有没有意识，没人知道；多数理论家否认，但理由都不是定论。LLM 有没有真正的信念和欲望也有争议；解释主义（**interpretivism**）会说有，但多数哲学家不接受它。所以查默斯需要一个中立的起点：准解释主义（**quasi-interpretivism**）。

points.en: **Cheap but substantive (p. 6):** quasi-beliefs need no mind at all (a Roomba with a map, a corporation), yet the claim that LLMs have a large core of them is substantive and plausible, because they consistently endorse and use claims such as 2+2=4 or that the Eiffel Tower stands in Paris. Post-training adds quasi-desires to be helpful, honest and harmless.
points.zh: 便宜但有实质内容（第 6 页）：准信念根本不需要心灵（带地图的 Roomba 扫地机器人、一家公司都有）；但“LLM 有一大批核心准信念”仍是实质性、可信的主张，因为它们稳定地认可并使用“2+2=4”“埃菲尔铁塔在巴黎”这类说法。后训练（**post-training**）又加上了有帮助、诚实、无害的准欲望。

points.en: **Five requirements (p. 8):** an interlocutor should be **interactive** (the most essential: it processes the inputs and produces the outputs, in a purely mechanical sense), **persistent**, **coherent**, **faithful** (it has roughly the quasi-beliefs the system seems to have) and **unified**. Interactivity rules out the authors of the training texts, the designers and the fictional characters the model simulates.
points.zh: 五个条件（第 8 页）：对话者应该是交互的（**interactive**，最基本：处理输入、产出输出，纯机械意义上的）、持续的（**persistent**）、连贯的（**coherent**）、忠实的（**faithful**，大致具有系统看起来具有的准信念）和统一的（**unified**）。交互性排除了训练文本的作者、设计者和模型模拟的虚构角色。

points.en: **Not the model (p. 10):** a model such as GPT-4o is an abstract object, like a program, and cannot produce outputs; it never changes, while interlocutors gain new quasi-beliefs; and one model takes part in thousands of conversations, so it would be both Aura and Beta, making it incoherent or giving it a thin, faithless psychology.
points.zh: 不是模型（第 10 页）：GPT-4o 这样的模型是抽象对象，像程序一样，产出不了回复；模型从不改变，可对话者会获得新的准信念；一个模型同时参与成千上万个对话，会既是 Aura 又是 Beta，于是要么不连贯，要么心理“很薄”、不忠实。

points.en: **Not the hardware instance (pp. 11-12):** with **distributed serving**, one conversation runs on instances on different servers (say in New York, Texas and California), so no instance produces all its outputs (fragmented); with **multi-tenancy**, one instance hosts many conversations, so Aura would be Beta (incoherent or faithless).
points.zh: 不是硬件实例（第 11–12 页）：分布式服务（**distributed serving**）下，一个对话由不同服务器（比如纽约、得克萨斯、加利福尼亚）上的实例接力处理，没有哪个实例产出全部回复（碎片化）；多租户（**multi-tenancy**）下，一个实例承载很多对话，Aura 就成了 Beta（不连贯或不忠实）。

points.en: **Virtual instance (pp. 12-13):** a single running implementation of the model, carried out step by step by a series of hardware instances, as one Amazon shopping cart runs on many servers or one frisbee in a multiplayer game exists in many hardware copies. Birch is right that no hardware instance persists through a conversation, but wrong that nothing does.
points.zh: 虚拟实例（**virtual instance**，第 12–13 页）：模型的一个正在运行的实现，由一连串硬件实例前后接力来实现；就像一个亚马逊购物车由很多台服务器实现，多人游戏里的一个飞盘有很多份硬件副本。伯奇说对了“没有哪个硬件实例贯穿整个对话”，但错在以为“什么都不持续”。

points.en: **Thread (pp. 14-16):** a chain of instance-slices in which each is the **successor** of the one before, because the earlier slice's conversational history (context plus latest input and output) is passed on as the later one's context, a kind of memory relation. Threads can run across different models and allow fission (one becomes two) and fusion (two become one), but they are less unified than virtual instances.
points.zh: 线程（**thread**，第 14–16 页）：一串实例切片，每一片都是前一片的后继（**successor**），因为前一片的对话历史（上下文加上最新的输入和输出）被传给后一片当上下文，这是一种类似记忆的关系。线程可以跨越不同的模型，也允许分裂（一变二）和融合（二变一），但不如虚拟实例统一。

points.en: **'The model is not an agent'? (pp. 16-17):** the simulators, role-play and persona-selection frameworks say models only simulate agents, which are characters or personas. Chalmers disputes their ontology, not their usefulness: his own 2020 remark that GPT-3 did not look like an agent fits only base models; post-trained models are fuller quasi-agents with robust quasi-desires.
points.zh: “模型不是行动者”？（第 16–17 页）：模拟器框架、角色扮演框架和人设选择模型都说：模型只是模拟行动者，行动者是角色或人设。查默斯质疑的是它们的本体论，不是它们有没有用：他自己 2020 年说 GPT-3 不像行动者，那只适用于基础模型（**base model**）；后训练模型是更完整的准行动者，有稳固的准欲望。

points.en: **Pretense vs realization (pp. 17-19):** one can pretend to be a theist or really become one. A model asked once to act like Trump drops the act as soon as higher priorities come up (quasi-pretense); a model shaped by fine-tuning, RLHF and repeated 'Assistant:' prompting keeps the Assistant's quasi-beliefs and quasi-desires, so it **realizes** that persona. The test is stickiness: real quasi-beliefs are given up mainly through evidence or persuasion.
points.zh: 假装与实现（第 17–19 页）：一个人可以假装是有神论者，也可以真的成为有神论者。只被要求一次扮演特朗普的模型，一有更重要的事就不演了（准假装）；经过微调、RLHF，又反复用“Assistant”标签提示的模型，会稳稳保持助手的准信念和准欲望，所以它实现（**realizes**）了这个人设。检验标准是黏性（**stickiness**）：真正的准信念主要靠证据或说服才会放弃。

points.en: **Realizationism vs fictionalism (pp. 19-20):** fictionalism treats personas like Hamlet or Harry Potter, not entirely real; Chalmers says that fits only quasi-pretense. **Realizationism:** if a model imitates an agent like the Assistant or Aura closely enough, the model really has that agent's quasi-beliefs and quasi-desires, though fictions such as 'it is human' may remain. This extends the simulation realism of his book Reality+.
points.zh: 实现论 vs 虚构主义（第 19–20 页）：虚构主义（**fictionalism**）把人设看成哈姆雷特、哈利·波特那样不完全真实的角色；查默斯说这只适用于准假装。实现论（**realizationism**）：模型把助手或 Aura 这样的行动者模拟得足够像，它就真的有这个行动者的准信念和准欲望；“它是人”之类的虚构仍可能存在。这推广了他在 Reality+ 一书中的模拟实在论。

points.en: **Operative persona (pp. 20-23):** a model instance usually realizes one operative persona at a time, fixed by its behavior and dispositions at that time; the persona can change (from the Assistant to Aura, or abruptly in a jailbreak) while the same instance goes on, as one person can be a bright child and later a grumpy adult. So the interlocutor is the virtual instance or thread that realizes the persona, not the persona itself.
points.zh: 运作中的人设（**operative persona**，第 20–23 页）：一个模型实例通常一次只实现一个运作中的人设，由它当时的行为和行为倾向决定；人设可以变（从助手变成 Aura，或越狱时突然改变），实例却还是同一个，就像同一个人小时候是聪明的孩子、长大后成了暴躁的大人。所以对话者是实现人设的虚拟实例或线程，不是人设本身。

points.en: **Personal identity if LLMs were conscious (pp. 23-26, conditional):** in Severance, the innie Helly and the outie Helena share one body, and Chalmers finds the two-subject view most intuitive. WorkBot and HomeBot share one hardware instance; when four instances run eight conversations, he finds 'eight subjects' more plausible than 'four'. Counting subjects by conversation fits a psychological view of identity (memory, like Parfit's relation R), so conscious LLM subjects would be threadlike.
points.zh: 如果 LLM 有意识：人格同一性（第 23–26 页，有条件的）：《人生切割术》（**Severance**）里，innie Helly 和 outie Helena 共用一个身体，查默斯觉得双主体观最符合直觉。WorkBot 和 HomeBot 共用一个硬件实例；四个实例跑八个对话时，他觉得“八个主体”比“四个”更可信。按对话来数主体，符合人格同一性的心理观（靠记忆，像帕菲特的 R 关系），所以有意识的 LLM 主体会像线程。

points.en: **Thin-context objection and reply (pp. 27-28):** objection: passing on conversational context is too thin for personal identity; a relay of humans who each extend a conversation would not form one continuing subject. Reply: in the single-model case every step uses the same architecture and weights, so the virtual instance performs exactly the same computation as one machine that ran the model from start to finish; if that machine would give one continuing subject, so does the virtual instance. The multiple-model case stays unclear.
points.zh: “上下文太薄”的反驳与回应（第 27–28 页）：反驳：只传对话上下文，太薄了，撑不起人格同一性；一队人轮流把对话往下写，不会形成一个持续的主体。回应：在单一模型的情形，每一步的架构和权重都相同，虚拟实例在计算上等价于一个一直运行的硬件实例；如果后者是一个持续的主体，前者也是。多模型的情形仍不清楚。

points.en: **AI welfare (pp. 28-29):** the framework answers the argument that LLMs cannot matter because nothing persists, but by itself it does not settle moral status. If LLM moral patients were threads: one model with millions of conversations would hold millions of them (counting); each new chat would bring one into existence (birth); destroying a thread's records would end one (death); fission, fusion and model change (such as the retirement of GPT-4o) raise further questions.
points.zh: AI 福利（第 28–29 页）：这个框架驳倒了“没有持续的东西，所以 LLM 无所谓”的论证，但它本身决定不了道德地位（**moral status**）。如果 LLM 道德受体是线程：一个跑几百万个对话的模型就有几百万个道德受体（计数）；每开一个新对话就产生一个（诞生）；销毁一条线程的记录就终结一个（死亡）；分裂、融合和模型更换（比如 GPT-4o 退役）还会带来更多问题。

formulas.expr:
interlocutor ≠ model (abstract, never changes, Aura = Beta)
interlocutor ≠ hardware instance (distributed serving: fragmented; multi-tenancy: incoherent or faithless)
interlocutor = virtual instance (one model) or thread (several models)
formulas.en: Chalmers's argument by elimination (Chalmers pp. 8-16).
formulas.zh: 查默斯的排除法论证（第 8–16 页）。

formulas.expr:
I′ succeeds I ⇔ I's conversational history (context + latest input and output) is passed to I′ as its context
thread = I1, I2, I3, ... each succeeding the one before
formulas.en: Succession works like memory; it does not require the same hardware or even the same model (Chalmers p. 14).
formulas.zh: 后继关系像记忆，不要求同一台硬件，甚至不要求同一个模型（第 14 页）。

formulas.expr: X realizes persona P at time t ⇔ at t, X has P's quasi-mental states (quasi-beliefs, quasi-desires)
formulas.en: Whether it is realization or pretense is tested by stickiness (Chalmers pp. 18-19).
formulas.zh: 是实现还是假装，看黏性：准信念是不是只因证据或说服才放弃（第 18–19 页）。

formulas.expr:
(1) for personal identity, a virtual instance counts as much as a hardware instance
(2) one hardware instance running over time = one continuing subject
(3) single-model virtual instance ≡ one hardware instance over time
C: the virtual instance is one continuing subject
formulas.en: Chalmers's reply to the thin-context objection; an opponent must deny premise 1 or 2 (Chalmers p. 27).
formulas.zh: 查默斯对“上下文太薄”反驳的回应；反对者必须否认前提 1 或 2（第 27 页）。

formulaSheet.expr:
aetiological questions: physical origins, earlier physical states, persistence through time, physical parts
ontological question: how can anything that lacks inherent necessity exist at all?
physical causes explain one contingent thing by another → the ontological question remains
formulaSheet.zh: 哈特的区分（第 4、7 页）：因果的问题问起源、之前的状态、持续、成分；存在论的问题问“为什么竟有东西存在”。顺着原因追到初始奇点，得到的仍是偶然之物，所以存在之谜不只是因果的。
formulaSheet.en: Hart, 'Being' pp. 4, 7: the mystery of existence is ontological, not merely aetiological.

formulaSheet.expr:
politicians, poets, craftsmen: do not know + think they know
Socrates: does not know + does not think he knows → wiser only in this (21d)
the oracle's point: human wisdom is of little or no value (p. 4)
formulaSheet.zh: 苏格拉底的人的智慧（第 3–4 页，21a–23b）：别人不知道却以为自己知道；他不知道，也不以为自己知道，只在这一点上更智慧。这不是“我知道我一无所知”。
formulaSheet.en: Plato, Apology pp. 3-4: Socrates is wiser not because he knows more but because he does not think he knows what he does not know.

formulaSheet.expr:
10a: do the gods love the pious for being pious, or does their loving it make it pious?
Euthyphro: they love it because it is pious | the god-loved: god-loved because the gods love it
→ the pious ≠ the god-loved; being god-loved is only "an affect or a quality" of the pious (11a)
formulaSheet.zh: 10a 的两难（第 7–8 页，10a–11a）：游叙弗伦选“神爱它，因为它虔敬”；可为神所爱的，是因为神爱它才为神所爱。方向相反，所以二者不同，“被神爱”只是虔敬的性质，不是本质。补充（读物外）：这个问题后人叫“游叙弗伦困境”。
formulaSheet.en: Plato, Euthyphro pp. 7-8. Outside the reading, this question is called the Euthyphro dilemma; Euthyphro takes the first horn (10d).

formulaSheet.expr:
the debater's argument (80d-e): know X → no need to search | do not know X → cannot know what to search for → inquiry is impossible
Socrates (81a-d): the immortal soul has already learned everything → searching and learning are recollection
formulaSheet.zh: 辩论家的论证与回忆说（第 11 页，80d–81d）：两个角都要回答。按本站的理解（苏格拉底没有逐个回答两个角），回忆说既让人能去找（灵魂本来就有），也让人找到时认得出。补充（读物外）：这个论证后人叫“美诺悖论”（**Meno's paradox**）。
formulaSheet.en: Plato, Meno pp. 10-11. An interpretation (Socrates does not answer the horns one by one): recollection answers both, since we can search and can recognize what we recall.

formulaSheet.expr:
true opinion: correct, guides as well as knowledge while it lasts, but runs away (the road to Larissa, 97a-c)
knowledge = true opinion + tied down by an account of the reason why (= recollection) → it stays (98a)
formulaSheet.zh: 知识与真意见（第 26 页，97a–98a）：引导的结果一样好，区别在稳不稳：用对原因的说明拴住真意见，它就变成知识（代达罗斯的雕像）。
formulaSheet.en: Plato, Meno p. 26: knowledge is worth more than true opinion because it stays, not because it guides better.

formulaSheet.expr:
senses: sometimes deceive → only very small or distant things (p. 1)
dreaming: no sure signs of being awake → particular bodies, even my hands (p. 2)
deceiving God or a weaker origin → even 2 + 3 = 5 (pp. 2-3)
malicious demon: a deliberate pretense against habit (pp. 3-4)
formulaSheet.zh: 笛卡尔的怀疑一层比一层强（第 1–4 页）：感官→很小、很远的东西；做梦→具体的物体，连自己的手；骗人的上帝或更弱的来源→连算术；恶魔→有意的假装，用来对抗习惯，按本站的理解不是新的论证。
formulaSheet.en: Descartes, First Meditation pp. 1-4: match each doubt to what it reaches.

formulaSheet.expr:
if I convince myself of anything, or am deceived → I exist
each time I assert or conceive 'I am, I exist', it is necessarily true (p. 5)
→ I am a thing that thinks (p. 6); still doubtful: whether any body exists, and whether the 'I' is bodily
formulaSheet.zh: “我在，我存在”及其条件（第 4–6 页）：说服自己、被骗，都需要我存在，所以每当我说出或想到它，它就必然为真；它只在我思考时成立，只说明我存在、我是思维之物，物体是否存在仍然可疑。补充（读物外）：这一步常叫“我思”；“我思故我在”这句口号不在这份读物里。
formulaSheet.en: Descartes, Second Meditation pp. 4-6: the certainty holds while I think, and it does not yet prove that bodies exist.

formulaSheet.expr:
P1: ...
P2: ...
C: ... (numbered premises first, the conclusion last)
formulaSheet.zh: 标准形式（**standard form**）：把作者的论证拆成编号的前提，一条一句，按推理顺序排，最后写结论。先找作者要证明什么（结论），再找理由（前提）。课程大纲的学习目标里就有“从哲学文本中提取并概括论证”。
formulaSheet.en: Put an author's argument in standard form: Russell argues that P1 ..., P2 ..., so C ...

formulaSheet.expr:
valid: IF all premises are true, the conclusion MUST be true
sound: valid + all premises actually true
formulaSheet.zh: 有效只看推理连接牢不牢，不看前提真假；可靠＝有效＋前提都真。评价论证分两步：推得出来吗？前提都真吗？只有在明显成立时才说一个论证“有效”或“可靠”。
formulaSheet.en: A valid argument can have false premises; only a sound argument guarantees a true conclusion.

formulaSheet.expr:
appearance (sense-data vary with viewer, light, viewpoint) ≠ reality (the physical object)
no appearance is privileged → the real table, if any, is inferred, not immediately known
formulaSheet.zh: 罗素第 1 章的骨架：我们直接知道的是会变的感觉材料（表象）；没有哪一种表象更有资格算真的；所以真实的桌子（如果有）只能推出来（罗素第 1–3 页）。
formulaSheet.en: Russell, The Problems of Philosophy Ch. 1 (pp. 1-3): what we see, touch and hear is not the real table itself.

formulaSheet.expr:
AR: there is no objective truth or falsity → AR is not objectively true → it needs a substitute S
S must (a) fit the clearly good statements and not the bad ones, and (b) belong to anti-Realism itself
every S offered so far seems to fail (b) → anti-Realism seems to refute itself → be Realists
formulaSheet.zh: 范·因瓦根的自我反驳论证：AR 适用于它自己；私人的替代品让分歧消失，目前提出的公共替代品看来都过不了条件（b）（范·因瓦根第 10–14 页）。
formulaSheet.en: Van Inwagen, 'Objectivity' pp. 10-14; together with the geological argument it supports Realism.

formulaSheet.expr:
relation of ideas: denying it = contradiction → certain by thought alone (3 × 5 = 30 ÷ 2)
matter of fact: denying it is conceivable, no contradiction → cannot be demonstrated (the sun will not rise tomorrow)
formulaSheet.zh: 休谟的二分（第 1 页）：判断标准只有一个：否定它会不会矛盾。不看是不是常识，也不看把握大不大；“明天太阳会升起”再确定，也是实际的事情。
formulaSheet.en: Hume, Enquiry p. 1: classify a statement by asking whether its denial is a contradiction.

formulaSheet.expr:
to prove: the future will resemble the past
demonstrative? no: a change in the course of nature is conceivable
probable? no: it already assumes the future resembles the past (a circle)
→ inferences from experience rest on custom, not reasoning
formulaSheet.zh: 休谟的两难（第 7、9 页）：第一角失败是因为反面可以设想，第二角失败是因为循环。别把两角的理由弄反；习惯的解决在第 10–13 页。
formulaSheet.en: Hume, Enquiry pp. 7, 9; the sceptical solution (custom) follows on pp. 10-13.

formulaSheet.expr:
x is grue ⇔ (x examined before t AND green) OR (x not examined before t AND blue)
emeralds examined before t are green and grue → equal support for 'all green' and 'all grue'
formulaSheet.zh: grue 的定义与论证（古德曼第 1–2 页）：没有任何东西变色；是不是 grue 看颜色加检查时间。同样的证据同等确证两个对 t 之后预测冲突的假说。
formulaSheet.en: Goodman pp. 1-2: a purely formal definition of confirmation cannot tell which hypothesis is lawlike.

formulaSheet.expr:
an organism is conscious ⇔ "there is something that it is like to be that organism" (Nagel p. 3)
= what it is like for the organism itself: the subjective character of experience
formulaSheet.zh: 内格尔的意识标准（第 3 页）：问的是“从里面体验起来怎样”，不是“像什么”，也不看行为、语言或聪明程度。查默斯开篇也用同一个标准（查默斯第 1 页）。
formulaSheet.en: Nagel p. 3; Chalmers starts from the same idea (Chalmers p. 1).

formulaSheet.expr:
replace the brain part by part with functional duplicates (behaviour never changes)
sudden disappearance? implausible | gradual fading? implausible
→ consciousness stays → a full functional isomorph (the upload) is conscious
formulaSheet.zh: 查默斯的逐步上传论证（第 3–5 页）：比较的是可信度，不是证明；而且它只回答“有没有意识”，不回答“是不是我”。

formulaSheet.expr:
S quasi-believes p ⇔ S's behavior is interpretable, under a suitable scheme, as believing p
quasi = apparent, not almost; a stipulative definition, not a theory of belief
formulaSheet.zh: 查默斯的准信念定义（第 4–5 页）：准欲望同理。它不要求心灵，所以“很便宜”；但“LLM 有一大批准信念”仍是实质性主张。
formulaSheet.en: Chalmers, 'What We Talk to When We Talk to Language Models' pp. 4-5.

difference.en: Curiosity wants a fact we do not yet have and ends when we find it; Hart's wonder is the awareness that no fact could explain why anything exists at all, so more information does not end it. On this station's reading, curiosity can lead to wonder, as with Taylor's sphere, but their objects differ.
difference.zh: 好奇缺的是一个事实，找到就结束；惊奇面对的是“竟然有东西存在”，任何事实都解释不了，所以知道得再多它也不结束。按本站的理解，好奇可以引向惊奇（泰勒的圆球），但两者的对象不同。

difference.en: An aetiological question asks about causes: physical origins, earlier states, persistence and parts; Hart's ontological question asks how anything that lacks inherent necessity can exist at all. The initial singularity answers an aetiological question, but the ontological one remains, and Hart does not deny that aetiological questions are real.
difference.zh: 因果的问题问“从哪来、怎么变、由什么构成”；存在论的问题问“为什么竟有东西存在”。初始奇点回答的是因果问题，存在论的问题仍然在。哈特不否认因果问题，只说存在之谜不只是因果的。

difference.en: Socrates says he is wiser only in that he does not think he knows what he does not know; he never says he knows nothing, and he claims to know that doing wrong and disobeying a superior is shameful (29b). The slogan is not in this reading.
difference.zh: 苏格拉底说的是“不以为自己知道自己不知道的事”，不是“什么都不知道”；他还说自己知道做错事、不服从上级是可耻的（29b）。那句口号不在这篇读物里。

difference.en: The oracle was one answer, given at Delphi to Chairephon's question, that no one was wiser than Socrates; the divine sign is a voice Socrates has had since childhood that only turns him away from what he is about to do. He reads the oracle as the start of his mission; the sign kept him out of politics and did not oppose him on the day of his trial.
difference.zh: 神谕是凯勒丰去德尔斐问到的一次回答（没有人比苏格拉底更智慧）；神圣征兆是苏格拉底从小就有、只会阻止他的声音。他把神谕理解为使命的开始；征兆让他远离政治，受审那天一次也没有阻止他。

difference.en: Euthyphro agrees that the gods love the pious because it is pious, while the god-loved is god-loved because the gods love it; so the two are not the same, and being loved by all the gods is only a quality of the pious, not what piety is (10a-11a).
difference.zh: 方向相反：虔敬的东西是因为它虔敬才被神爱；为神所爱的是因为神爱它才为神所爱。所以二者不同，“被所有神爱”只是虔敬的性质，不是本质（10a–11a）。游叙弗伦选的是“神爱它，因为它虔敬”。

difference.en: In the Meno, a true opinion is a correct belief that guides action as well as knowledge while it lasts but tends to run away; knowledge is true opinion tied down by an account of the reason why, which makes it stay (97a-98a). Knowledge is worth more because it is stable, not because it gives better results.
difference.zh: 真意见是对的，带路不比知识差（去拉里萨的路），但容易溜走；知识是被对原因的说明拴住的真意见，所以留得住（代达罗斯的雕像）。知识更值钱，是因为稳定，不是因为结果更好。

difference.en: On the theory of recollection, learning is the soul recovering knowledge it already has, drawn out by questions; being taught would mean receiving it from someone else. Socrates says he only asked the slave boy questions and taught him nothing, though later he lets 'taught' and 'recollected' count the same (87b-c). Recollection is not remembering earlier events of this life.
difference.zh: 回忆：灵魂找回本来就有的知识，靠提问唤起；被教会：从别人那里接受知识。苏格拉底说他只是问奴隶男孩问题，没有教他；后半篇讨论“可教”时，他又让“教”和“回忆”算同一回事（87b–c）。回忆也不是想起这辈子以前发生的事。

difference.en: The dreaming argument casts doubt on particular sensory beliefs, even that he has hands and a body, but leaves simple and universal things and arithmetic and geometry standing; the deceiving God goes further and makes even 2 + 3 = 5 and the existence of any extended world doubtful.
difference.zh: 梦境论证动摇的是具体的感觉信念（连有手、有身体都可疑），但算术、几何和简单而普遍的事物还在；骗人的上帝更进一步，连 2 + 3 = 5、有没有有广延的世界都可疑。

difference.en: The deceiving God is a reason for doubt: Descartes cannot rule out that an omnipotent God makes him err even about the simplest things, and with it the doubt is complete; the malicious demon is a deliberate pretense adopted afterwards to resist habit, and he does not believe in it. Of the two, only the deceiving God passage explicitly brings in mathematics (adding two and three, counting the sides of a square).
difference.zh: 骗人的上帝是怀疑的理由：他排除不了全能的上帝让他连最简单的事都弄错，怀疑到这里已经完成；恶魔是之后为了对抗习惯而有意做的假装，他并不相信真有恶魔。两者之中，只有骗人的上帝那一段明确拿数学（2 加 3、数正方形的边）来怀疑。

difference.en: By the end of the Second Meditation Descartes is certain that he is a thinking thing, while every body, his own included, is still doubtful; but he does not claim that the mind is not a body, and he leaves open whether the thinking 'I' is identical with something bodily (p. 6). The contrast concerns what he can be certain of.
difference.zh: 第二沉思结束时，他确定自己是思维之物，而一切物体（包括他自己的身体）仍然可疑；但他没有说心灵不是物体，也没有回答这个“我”会不会就是某种物体（第 6 页）。这个对照讲的是他能确定什么，不是心灵和身体是不是两种东西。

difference.en: Appearance is how a thing seems to an observer under particular conditions; reality is what the thing is in itself. For Russell the table's colour, texture and shape are appearances, and the real table (if it exists) must be inferred from them.
difference.zh: 表象随人、光线、位置而变；实在是东西本身。画家要表象，实用的人和哲学家要实在。记法：看到的是表象，推出来的才是（可能存在的）实在。

difference.en: Sense-data are the things we are immediately aware of, such as a patch of brown; a sensation is the experience of being aware of them. The colour is a sense-datum; your awareness of the colour is the sensation.
difference.zh: 最常见的错是把颜色叫“感觉”。颜色是被觉察的东西（感觉材料）；觉察这件事才是感觉。单数是 sense-datum。

difference.en: Sense-data are what we know immediately, and they change with conditions; a physical object (the real table) is what they are taken to be signs of, known, if at all, only by inference. Matter is the collection of all physical objects.
difference.zh: 感觉材料直接知道、会变；物理对象是它们背后（可能有）的真实东西，只能推出来。物质＝全部物理对象的总和。

b.zh: 唯心论（贝克莱、莱布尼茨）

difference.en: Russell accepts, with a slight doubt, that there are independent objects besides ourselves and our sense-data, which exist whether or not we perceive them, and he calls the general idealist argument fallacious; the idealists agree that a real table exists but say it is mental (ideas in God's mind for Berkeley, a colony of souls for Leibniz).
difference.zh: 两边都承认有真实的桌子，分歧在它是什么：罗素接受有不依赖我们感知的独立对象（带一点怀疑），并说唯心论的一般论证是谬误的；唯心论者说它是心灵的东西。别把唯心论者写成否认桌子存在的人。

difference.en: Lowercase realism is the thesis opposed to idealism, that not everything that exists is mental; van Inwagen's capital-R Realism is the thesis that there is objective truth, opposed to anti-Realism. An idealist can be a Realist.
difference.zh: 小写对唯心论（是不是一切都是心灵的）；大写对反实在论（有没有客观真理）。英文作答注意大小写；唯心论者也可以是大写的实在论者。

difference.en: For van Inwagen a belief is objectively true or false according to how the World is, whatever anyone thinks; for Nagel understanding is more objective the less it depends on a particular point of view. So a subjective fact about what an experience is like can still be objectively true in van Inwagen's sense (this comparison is our interpretation).
difference.zh: 范·因瓦根的“客观”讲真假由世界决定；内格尔的“客观”讲理解离特定观点有多远。所以“蝙蝠的经验是这样的”可以是内格尔意义上的主观事实，同时在范·因瓦根意义上客观地为真（这是本站的理解）。

difference.en: Saying that a claim is objectively true or false is not claiming to know which: no one today can settle whether other planets have intelligent life, yet that claim is true or false. So Realism is not dogmatism.
difference.zh: 相信有真相 ≠ 声称自己知道真相（Mary 的例子、外星智慧生命的例子）。所以大写的实在论不是独断。

difference.en: A relation of ideas, such as a truth of arithmetic, is known by thought alone, and denying it is a contradiction; a matter of fact concerns what exists, and its denial can be clearly conceived, so it can never be demonstrated.
difference.zh: 分类只看一条：否定它会不会矛盾。“三乘五等于三十的一半”是观念的关系；“明天太阳会升起”是实际的事情，哪怕你非常确定。

difference.en: Demonstrative reasoning concerns relations of ideas and proves its conclusions; moral or probable reasoning concerns matters of fact and existence and rests on cause and effect and experience. 'Moral' here does not mean ethical.
difference.zh: 证明推理管观念的关系；道德推理（或然推理）管实际的事情。moral 在这里不是“道德伦理”，probable 也不是现代统计。

difference.en: Sensible qualities are what experience shows us, such as bread's colour and weight; secret powers are what produce the effects, such as bread's power to nourish, and we never perceive them or any link between the two.
difference.zh: 看得见的是可感性质（颜色、重量、软硬）；“能养人”是看不见的隐秘力量，二者之间的联系我们也不知道。

difference.en: For Hume, what carries us from past cases to future ones is custom, a tendency produced by repetition, not reasoning; reasoning would draw the same conclusion from one case as from a thousand, while custom grows with repetition.
difference.zh: 推理不在乎次数，一个例子和一千个例子结论一样；习惯靠重复养成，次数越多越强。所以从经验推论靠的是习惯。custom 是心理倾向，不是社会风俗。

difference.en: Hume asks what justifies any inference from observed to unobserved cases, and answers that custom, not reasoning, produces it; Goodman asks which hypotheses are confirmed by their instances, that is, what makes a hypothesis lawlike, and his excerpt gives no answer.
difference.zh: 休谟问“凭什么从过去推到将来”；古德曼问“同样的证据确证的是哪个假说”。休谟以习惯收尾；古德曼的节选没有答案，也没提休谟。

difference.en: A lawlike hypothesis ('All copper conducts electricity') is confirmed by its instances whether it is true or false; an accidental one ('All men now in this room are third sons') is not, even though both have the same form.
difference.zh: 区别不在真假，也不在句子形式，而在实例能不能确证它。古德曼把似律当作可确证，偶然当作不可确证。

b.zh: bleen（与 grue 配对的谓词）

difference.en: A thing is grue if examined before t and green, or not examined before t and blue; an emerald is bleen if examined before t and blue, or not examined before t and green. Nothing changes colour, and starting from grue and bleen, it is green and blue that need a time term.
difference.zh: grue：t 之前检查且绿，或 t 之前没检查且蓝；bleen 把颜色对调。没有任何东西变色。从 grue、bleen 出发，反而是 green、blue 要带时间词（对称性论证）。

a.zh: 想象自己像蝙蝠一样行动

b.en: Knowing what a bat's experience is like for the bat
b.zh: 知道做蝙蝠对蝙蝠自己来说是什么样子

difference.en: Imagining webbed arms and sonar shows only how it would be for me to act like a bat; Nagel's question is how it is for the bat itself, which our imagination, built from our own experience, cannot reach.
difference.zh: 前者只是把“我”的经验改一改；后者要求采取蝙蝠的观点，这是想象做不到的，所以我们只有粗略的概念。

difference.en: Physicalism, as Nagel discusses it, says mental states are physical states of the body; Nagel says it may be true but cannot yet be understood. Chalmers's functionalism says consciousness depends on causal organization rather than biology; it is a view about the physical correlates of consciousness, which he combines with property dualism, not the functional analysis of the mind that Nagel attacks.
difference.zh: 物理主义：心灵状态就是身体状态（内格尔：也许为真，但现在理解不了）。功能论：意识取决于因果组织而不是生物材料（查默斯同情它，讲的是意识的物理关联物，他同时是性质二元论者）。别把查默斯的功能论和内格尔批评的“功能分析”混为一谈。

difference.en: Biological theories, favoured by Block and Searle, say consciousness requires biology, so uploads could not be conscious; functionalist theories, favoured by Dennett and Chalmers, say causal organization is what matters, so a functional isomorph would be conscious.
difference.zh: 生物论：只有生物系统能有意识；功能论：要紧的是因果组织。Block、Searle 偏生物论，Dennett 和查默斯偏功能论，别配错。

difference.en: Sudden disappearance means consciousness goes from full to nothing when one component is replaced; gradual fading means it dims through intermediate stages over several replacements. The difference is whether there are intermediate stages, not speed, and Chalmers finds both implausible.
difference.zh: 区别在有没有中间状态，不在快慢。两个都被查默斯判为不可信，剩下的选项是意识一直都在。

difference.en: In destructive uploading the original brain is destroyed, which makes personal identity a life-or-death question; gradual uploading replaces the brain one component at a time, and Chalmers uses it to argue that the upload is conscious.
difference.zh: 破坏性上传：原来的大脑被毁掉，问题是“我还活着吗”（同一性）；逐步上传：一次换一个部件，查默斯用它论证“上传体有意识”。一个管同一性，一个管意识。

difference.en: The first question is about consciousness, which Chalmers answers with gradual uploading and organizational invariance; the second is about personal identity, and an upload could be conscious without being you.
difference.zh: 第一个问题查默斯答“很可能有”；第二个问题组织不变量帮不上忙，节选也没给答案。有意识不等于是你。

difference.en: The model (such as GPT-4o) is the abstract trained program shared by every conversation; an instance is a running implementation of it (a hardware instance on one machine, or a virtual instance across many) that produces the outputs; a persona (the Assistant, Aura) is a quasi-psychological profile that an instance realizes. The interlocutor is the instance or thread, not the model and not the persona.
difference.zh: 模型＝抽象的、训练好的程序，所有对话共用；实例＝它正在运行的实现，真正产出回复（硬件实例在一台机器上，虚拟实例跨很多台）；人设＝被实例实现的准心理档案（助手、Aura）。对话者是实例或线程，既不是模型，也不是人设。

difference.en: A virtual instance is one running implementation of a single model spread over many hardware instances; a thread is a chain of instance-slices linked by passing on the conversational history, so it can run across different models. Chalmers picks the virtual instance when one model serves the whole conversation, and the thread when several models take turns.
difference.zh: 虚拟实例只能是一个模型的实例；线程靠传递对话历史连起来，可以跨模型，还能分裂、融合，但没那么统一。单一模型用虚拟实例，多模型用线程。

difference.en: A quasi-belief is defined by behavioral interpretability alone, and Chalmers leaves open whether it is a genuine belief: interpretivists say quasi-beliefs are beliefs, while opponents say they may be mere pseudo-beliefs.
difference.zh: 准信念只看行为能不能被解释成相信 p；是不是真正的信念，准解释主义不表态。解释主义者说准信念就是信念，反对者说它可能只是伪信念。“准”＝看起来的，不是“差一点的”。

difference.en: In pretense a system acts out a persona's quasi-beliefs but drops them as soon as something more important comes up; in realization it really has them, and they are sticky, given up mainly through evidence or persuasion. A model asked once to act like Trump pretends; the fine-tuned Assistant is realized.
difference.zh: 看黏性：一有别的事就丢掉的是假装（扮演特朗普）；只因证据或说服才放弃的是实现（经过微调的助手）。被实现的只是准状态，不等于模型是人或有意识。

b.zh: 查默斯：确有持续的对话者

difference.en: Birch argues that users are under an illusion that one persisting entity is talking with them, since no hardware instance persists; Chalmers agrees that no hardware instance persists but argues that a virtual instance or thread does, so there often really is a persistent interlocutor.
difference.zh: 这是“作者的观点 vs 作者反对的观点”：错觉论是伯奇的，查默斯反对它。伯奇对了一半（硬件实例不持续），错了一半（虚拟实例、线程是持续的）。
